drugs.use: Alternative oral agent for mild-moderate COVID-19 in high-risk adults when the preferred agent cannot be used; shortens recovery but does not reduce hospitalization

drugs.name: Montelukast
drugs.mechanism: Blocks leukotriene receptors, countering the leukotriene rise that follows COX-1 inhibition (less PGE2, more leukotrienes, mucosal edema)
drugs.use: Asthma with nasal polyps that worsens 20 minutes to 3 hours after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs

drugs.name: Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir (Paxlovid)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits the SARS-CoV-2 3CL protease, so viral polyproteins are not cleaved; the co-packaged pill inhibits CYP3A4 so the antiviral is not inactivated (pharmacokinetic booster)
drugs.adverseEffects: Bad taste (dysgeusia), nausea, diarrhea, rash; liver enzyme rise and hypersensitivity from the booster; boxed warning for major CYP3A4 drug-drug interactions; renal dose adjustment
drugs.use: Preferred oral antiviral for mild-moderate COVID-19 in a high-risk outpatient (12+), within 5 days of symptoms after an interaction check; no second course for rebound

drugs.name: NSAIDs (ketorolac, ibuprofen)
drugs.mechanism: Nonselective COX inhibition blocks prostaglandin synthesis, so the kidney loses vasodilatory prostaglandins; COX-2-selective drugs spare the gut but still affect the COX-2-rich kidney
drugs.adverseEffects: Ischemic AKI with papillary necrosis at high doses; hypersensitivity interstitial nephritis, sometimes with minimal change nephrotic syndrome; hyperkalemia in CKD; bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive asthma
drugs.use: First-line analgesic for renal colic (opioids only occasionally, e.g. significant renal impairment); avoided in CKD and stopped 24-48 h before iodinated contrast

drugs.name: Omalizumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against IgE, so less IgE arms the high-affinity receptors on mast cells that allergens cross-link to release histamine
drugs.use: Specialist-started add-on for severe allergic (IgE-mediated) asthma that stays uncontrolled despite adherence, good inhaler technique and a confirmed diagnosis

drugs.name: OnabotulinumtoxinA (botulinum toxin)
drugs.mechanism: Injected into the detrusor, it blocks acetylcholine release and relaxes the bladder
drugs.adverseEffects: Can paralyze the bladder, so the patient may have to self-catheterize
drugs.use: Urge incontinence that persists despite lifestyle change and anticholinergic drugs; sacral nerve modulation and bladder augmentation are the other later options

drugs.name: Oseltamivir
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug; blood and tissue esterases form the active carboxylate, which blocks neuraminidase so new virions clump on the cell surface (influenza A and B); renally secreted, so adjust for renal impairment
drugs.adverseEffects: Nausea and vomiting (taking it with food helps), headache, serious skin reactions; no metabolism-related drug interactions expected
drugs.use: Drug of choice for influenza treatment and prophylaxis at any age, outpatient or inpatient, and in pregnancy; start within 48 hours; twice daily for 5 days

drugs.name: Oxybutynin / tolterodine
drugs.mechanism: Anticholinergics that block muscarinic receptors on the detrusor, damping the involuntary contractions of an overactive bladder
drugs.adverseEffects: Dry mouth, constipation, dry eyes, blurred vision, orthostatic hypotension, fast heart rate; cross the blood-brain barrier (caution in the elderly); avoid in heart disease and closed-angle glaucoma
drugs.use: Urge incontinence from detrusor overactivity after lifestyle measures; the urge component of mixed incontinence

drugs.name: Penicillin and aminopenicillins (amoxicillin, ampicillin)
drugs.mechanism: Beta-lactams that inhibit the transpeptidases (PBPs) cross-linking peptidoglycan; useless against wall-less Mycoplasma and against MRSA's mecA-encoded PBP2a; clavulanate added against beta-lactamase
drugs.use: Strep pharyngitis with 4 Centor points (no test needed); first-line bacterial sinusitis and healthy-outpatient CAP; actinomycosis; 7 days for bacteriuria in pregnancy; neonatal UTI with gentamicin

drugs.name: Peramivir
drugs.mechanism: Neuraminidase inhibitor given intravenously, a single dose for outpatients; excreted unchanged by the kidney (renal dose adjustment); half-life about 20 h
drugs.adverseEffects: Hyperglycemia, diarrhea or constipation, serious skin and hypersensitivity reactions; give only where infusion reactions can be treated
drugs.use: Influenza in a patient who cannot take or absorb the oral first-line agent; treatment only, never prophylaxis

drugs.name: Potassium citrate
drugs.mechanism: Complexes calcium in the urine, lowering calcium saturation, crystal growth and aggregation; the body's own stone inhibitor is low in renal tubular acidosis, strenuous exercise and high-animal-protein diets
drugs.use: Calcium phosphate stones, alongside a low-sodium diet and a thiazide

drugs.name: Pramipexole / ropinirole
drugs.mechanism: Dopaminergic agonists: stimulate dopamine receptors directly, rather than supplying the dopamine precursor as levodopa does
drugs.use: Long-standing drug of choice for unpleasant evening leg sensations that start at rest, force the patient to get up and move, and ease only while walking; gabapentin is a listed alternative

drugs.name: Pretomanid
drugs.mechanism: Nitroimidazole prodrug activated by the mycobacterial Ddn nitroreductase; releases nitric oxide and reactive nitrogen species that break down the mycolic acid wall; long half-life
drugs.adverseEffects: Peripheral neuropathy, QT prolongation and hepatotoxicity; baseline and regular ECGs and periodic liver tests through the roughly 6-month course
drugs.use: Pulmonary XDR-TB, or MDR-TB that is treatment-intolerant or nonresponsive, given with bedaquiline and linezolid for about 6 months

drugs.name: Pyrazinamide
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug: mycobacterial pyrazinamidase (pncA gene) makes pyrazinoic acid, which lowers intracellular pH and disrupts membranes and fatty acid synthesis; bactericidal on replicating bacilli. Resistance: pncA mutation
drugs.adverseEffects: Marked hepatotoxicity (mitochondrial oxidative stress), additive with isoniazid and rifampin; hyperuricemia from reduced uric acid excretion, which can flare gout
drugs.use: Only the first 2 months (8 weeks) of active TB therapy, then stopped; left out of the pregnancy regimen

drugs.name: Remdesivir
drugs.mechanism: Adenosine nucleotide analog prodrug, triphosphorylated and incorporated by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase; the chain stops two or three nucleotides later (delayed chain termination)
drugs.adverseEffects: Severe bradycardia (mechanism unknown); reversible aminotransferase rise; hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis, angioedema; hyperglycemia; chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine lowers its effect
drugs.use: IV for COVID-19 in hospitalized patients not on mechanical ventilation (usually 5 days) or high-risk outpatients (3 days); infants of 3 kg and up; only where infusion reactions can be treated

drugs.name: Rifabutin
drugs.mechanism: Same RNA polymerase target and red secretions as the parent rifamycin, but much weaker CYP induction; hepatotoxicity similar; reduce the dose when CrCl is below 30 mL/min
drugs.use: Replaces the standard rifamycin in TB patients taking antiretroviral therapy, to avoid induction interactions; optional third drug for MAC in advanced HIV

drugs.name: Rifampin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; resistance from an altered polymerase. Daily dosing; a strong CYP3A4 inducer; distributes widely into body fluids; covers gram-positive, gram-negative and acid-fast bacteria
drugs.adverseEffects: Red-orange urine, tears and saliva (harmless once blood is excluded; shows adherence); hepatitis, worse with isoniazid or pyrazinamide; induces CYP3A4, so oral contraceptives and HIV drugs fail
drugs.use: Four-drug TB therapy, then continued 4 more months; 4 months alone for latent TB; prophylaxis for close contacts of meningococcal or H. influenzae disease (dorm, jail), not meningitis treatment

drugs.name: Rifapentine
drugs.mechanism: Rifamycin RNA polymerase inhibitor with a long half-life that allows once-weekly dosing; still a potent CYP inducer
drugs.use: Weekly with isoniazid for 3 months as a latent TB option in HIV (CD4 < 200); part of the newer 4-month active TB regimen with isoniazid, pyrazinamide and moxifloxacin

drugs.name: Rimantadine
drugs.mechanism: M2 proton channel blocker (influenza A only) with low CNS distribution and extensive hepatic hydroxylation and conjugation; excreted as metabolites; half-life highly variable (13-65 h)
drugs.adverseEffects: CNS effects such as insomnia and poor concentration occur less often than with its brain-penetrating relative

drugs.name: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin)
drugs.mechanism: Block sodium-glucose cotransport in the proximal tubule, lowering blood glucose and reducing glomerular hyperfiltration
drugs.use: Slow CKD progression (strongest evidence alongside RAS blockade); in CKD with heart failure they help regardless of albuminuria; in type 2 diabetes, fewer cardiovascular events and weight loss

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate
drugs.mechanism: Extra buffer outside cells pulls H+ out in exchange for K+ moving in; used to alkalinize the urine (not the serum), so some toxins leave faster and some stones form less readily
drugs.adverseEffects: Not for DKA (worse outcomes in studies), rhabdomyolysis (fewer myoglobin casts but no AKI or mortality benefit) or simply an unwanted pH number
drugs.use: Hyperkalemia; tricyclic and other Na+ channel blocker overdose; urine alkalinization in salicylate overdose; oral alkali in CKD acidosis to keep serum HCO3- above 23

drugs.name: Sodium oxybate (GHB)
drugs.adverseEffects: Itself a drug of abuse that also circulates illicitly, so prescribers need special training; leave it to sleep specialists
drugs.use: Narcolepsy: the one drug listed both for daytime sleepiness and for collapses triggered by laughter or strong emotion

drugs.name: Supplemental O2
drugs.adverseEffects: In a chronic CO2 retainer, too much can push PaCO2 higher and depress breathing (taught as loss of hypoxic drive), so titrate to a modest saturation
drugs.use: The one COPD therapy proven to improve mortality and survival; in an exacerbation, give only enough to correct the hypoxemia

drugs.name: Systemic corticosteroids (prednisone)
drugs.adverseEffects: Suppress host defenses, raising the risk of invasive aspergillosis in immunocompromised patients; a cause of metabolic alkalosis
drugs.use: IV in status asthmaticus; oral, with albuterol, for a COPD exacerbation; first line for progressive sarcoidosis; desquamative interstitial pneumonia and eosinophilic pneumonias

drugs.name: Tecovirimat
drugs.mechanism: Stops newly made orthopoxvirus particles from being released from infected cells
drugs.use: FDA-approved for smallpox; used off-label for severe mpox alongside supportive care and pain control

drugs.name: Thalidomide
drugs.mechanism: Lowers TNF-alpha and decreases angiogenesis; a racemic drug whose (S) enantiomer is the teratogen
drugs.adverseEffects: Short or absent limb long bones (phocomelia) after first-trimester exposure; requires pregnancy tests at the start and during therapy and two forms of birth control
drugs.use: Erythema nodosum leprosum, the severe inflammatory reaction of leprosy; multiple myeloma

drugs.name: Thiazide diuretics
drugs.mechanism: Block the NaCl cotransporter of the distal convoluted tubule and increase distal calcium reabsorption, so less calcium reaches the urine
drugs.use: Prevent recurrent calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate stones, with a low-sodium (not low-calcium) diet; stopped at least 24 h before iodinated contrast

drugs.name: Third-generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime)
drugs.mechanism: Beta-lactam transpeptidase (PBP) inhibitors with broad gram-negative reach; resistance now spreading in E. coli, K. pneumoniae and gonococci; enterococci are intrinsically resistant
drugs.use: Empiric bacterial meningitis; IM dose for gonorrhea; febrile infant UTI (IM or IV); epiglottitis; inpatient CAP with a macrolide; acute pyelonephritis

drugs.name: Tiopronin / penicillamine
drugs.mechanism: Chelating agents that bind cystine and help dissolve the stones
drugs.use: Inherited stone disease with hexagonal crystals that keeps recurring despite a low-sodium diet, high fluids and urine alkalinization

drugs.name: Tirzepatide
drugs.mechanism: Agonist at incretin receptors, the GLP-1 receptor among them, that produces weight loss; whether it improves the airway beyond the weight lost is not known
drugs.use: Moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity: lowered AHI, weight, hypoxic burden, CRP and systolic BP (2024 trial); first drug FDA-approved for this mechanical disease

drugs.name: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX)
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate blockade: the sulfonamide (a PABA analog) inhibits dihydropteroate synthase and its partner inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, so no tetrahydrofolate for DNA synthesis
drugs.use: 3 days for uncomplicated cystitis (10-14 if complicated); drug of choice for Pneumocystis pneumonia; sinusitis or epiglottitis in penicillin allergy or suspected S. aureus

drugs.name: Vaginal / topical estrogen
drugs.mechanism: Restores the hormone-dependent support of the bladder neck and urethral tissues that weakens after menopause ('plumps the area back up')
drugs.use: Stress incontinence in a perimenopausal or recently postmenopausal woman; cream for symptomatic labial adhesions in a girl, for 2-3 weeks until they separate

drugs.name: Vancomycin
drugs.mechanism: Glycopeptide that binds the D-alanine-D-alanine end of peptidoglycan precursors, blocking cell wall polymer assembly after the alanine racemase step; resistance now seen in E. faecium and some S. aureus
drugs.use: IV for MRSA, including MRSA HAP/VAP; given orally, with fidaxomicin as the other first-line choice, for C. difficile colitis; with imipenem and an aminoglycoside for severe HAP

drugs.name: Zanamivir
drugs.mechanism: Neuraminidase inhibitor inhaled as a dry powder; low systemic absorption (about 4-17%), minimal metabolism, no renal dose adjustment listed
drugs.adverseEffects: Bronchospasm in asthma or COPD (an inhaled powder that is not a bronchodilator); headache, sinusitis, dizziness, ear-nose-throat infections; oropharyngeal or facial edema
drugs.use: Outpatient influenza treatment from age 7 and prophylaxis from age 5 in someone who can manage an inhaler; not recommended with underlying airway disease

correlates.name: Actinomycosis
correlates.presentation: 46-year-old man with many decayed teeth who had a lower molar pulled 6 weeks ago. A firm, slowly enlarging swelling at the angle of the jaw now drains pus through the skin; 3 weeks of low fever and cough. T 37.9 C; hard, painless jaw mass with a draining tract.
correlates.workup: Pus contains hard yellow grains made of tangled gram-positive branching filaments; not acid-fast; grows only anaerobically and is catalase-negative. Chest film: right lower lobe infiltrate.
correlates.management: Penicillin; fix the dental disease, since the organism is normal mouth flora that reaches the lung when aspirated.

correlates.name: Acute bacterial prostatitis
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old man has 2 days of fever, frequency, burning on urination, trouble starting his stream and aching in the perineum and low back. T 101.3 F, other vitals stable. Rectal exam: a tense, swollen, exquisitely tender gland; pus appears at the meatus.
correlates.workup: Urine: more than 10 WBC per high-power field; the voided urine culture is positive, most often for a gram-negative enteric rod.
correlates.management: A fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin or norfloxacin) for 2-4 weeks; TMP-SMX only once sensitivities are known. The trap is treating it as a bladder infection for 3-7 days - if symptoms persist, go back and examine the gland.

correlates.name: Acute bacterial sinusitis
correlates.presentation: 35-year-old man whose cold 2 weeks ago never cleared despite over-the-counter decongestants. Sinus pressure, blocked nose, thick purulent nasal discharge, frontal headache, facial pain worse on bending forward. T 37.6 C; tender over both maxillary sinuses.
correlates.management: Amoxicillin (TMP-SMX if severe penicillin allergy), plus antihistamines or nasal steroids for symptoms. CT only if complicated; watch for bone infection, meningitis or brain abscess.

correlates.name: Acute drug-induced tubulointerstitial nephritis
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old woman started trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a skin infection 15 days ago: fever, a diffuse red rash and less urine. Temp 100.9 F, BP 128/80. Eosinophils 11%. Creatinine 0.9 rising to 2.8 mg/dL. UA WBCs without bacteria, trace protein.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: interstitial edema with lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils and many eosinophils; leukocytes infiltrating tubule walls (tubulitis), worst in the medulla where the drug concentrates
correlates.management: Stop the culprit drug at once (sulfonamides, methicillin, ampicillin, rifampin, diuretics, cimetidine are the usual ones) and do not re-expose

correlates.name: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A previously healthy 24-year-old man has fever, cough and rapidly worsening dyspnea over 4 days; no transfusion, aspiration, travel, animal contact or new drug. RR 34, SpO2 82% on air; he is intubated. Chest film: diffuse bilateral opacities; viral PCR, blood cultures negative.
correlates.workup: BAL: eosinophils 38% of cells, cultures and stains negative. Transbronchial biopsy: hyaline membranes lining the alveoli with many eosinophils in the walls and airspaces.
correlates.management: Ventilatory support plus high-dose systemic corticosteroids; the response is rapid.

correlates.name: Acute mountain sickness
correlates.presentation: A 31-year-old trekker flies in and climbs to 4,100 m in two days on the way to a Himalayan base camp. On the second night she has a throbbing headache, nausea and cannot sleep. HR 106, RR 22, SpO2 84% on air; lungs clear, gait steady.
correlates.management: Prevent it with acetazolamide started before the ascent: the drug's mild metabolic acidosis drives a compensatory rise in minute ventilation, raising alveolar oxygen and gas exchange.

correlates.name: Acute pyelonephritis
correlates.presentation: A 26-year-old woman had 3 days of burning and frequency; today she has T 39.4 C with shaking chills, nausea, two episodes of vomiting and right flank pain. HR 112, BP 118/72. Striking the right angle between the 12th rib and the spine reproduces the pain.
correlates.workup: Urine: leukocyte esterase and nitrite positive, many white cells and bacteria, white cell casts. WBC 16,500. CT (if done): an area of darker, poorly enhancing kidney.
correlates.management: Send a urine culture, then start a bactericidal broad-spectrum drug at once (fluoroquinolone, third-generation cephalosporin, aminoglycoside). Admit for intractable vomiting, shock or dehydration; 10+ days; image if no better at 72 h.

correlates.name: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man admitted 2 days ago with severe acute pancreatitis grows steadily more breathless over 12 hours. RR 34, HR 120, BP 104/64, SpO2 86% on a 60% face mask. Crackles throughout both lungs; neck veins flat, no leg edema.
correlates.workup: PaO2 60 mm Hg on FiO2 0.6 (ratio 100); chest film: dense opacities in both lungs, no pleural effusions; wedge pressure 10 mm Hg; echo shows a normally contracting left ventricle.
correlates.management: Treat the trigger; low tidal volumes of 4-8 mL/kg; PEEP of at least 5 cm H2O, probably more; judicious fluids; prone positioning. No drug has been shown to lower mortality.

correlates.name: Acute silicosis (silicoproteinosis)
correlates.presentation: A 28-year-old who has sandblasted ship hulls in an enclosed dry dock for 7 months with a loose paper mask has 8 weeks of rapidly worsening dyspnea, dry cough and pleuritic chest pain. RR 28, SpO2 86% on room air, diffuse fine crackles.
correlates.workup: Chest film: bilateral diffuse hazy opacities without nodules or node calcification, appearing within months of a very heavy, fine, freshly fractured dust exposure.

correlates.name: Acute uncomplicated cystitis
correlates.presentation: A healthy 29-year-old woman has 2 days of burning on urination, urgency and going every hour; her urine looks cloudy and smells strong. No medicines, no past history. BP 100/70, HR 90, T 98.0 F. No back or flank tenderness, abdomen nontender, pelvic exam normal.
correlates.workup: Office dipstick: nitrite and leukocyte esterase positive; microscopy shows white cells and bacteria but no white cell casts. No imaging, CBC or metabolic panel needed.
correlates.management: With a good story and a positive dipstick, treat empirically: TMP-SMX for 3 days (sulfa allergy: nitrofurantoin 5-7 days or a fluoroquinolone 3 days). Send a culture if the dipstick is unimpressive or local resistance is high.

correlates.name: Acute uric acid nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old boy with newly diagnosed lymphoma, 2 days into induction chemotherapy: urine output falls to 200 mL/day. BP 118/76. Serum urate 18 mg/dL; creatinine 0.5 rising to 3.1 mg/dL. Urine pH 5.0 with many crystals.
correlates.workup: Serum urate 18 mg/dL with low-pH urine full of crystals. Pathology: precipitated crystals plugging the collecting tubules and obstructing nephrons, from purines released by lysed tumor cells

correlates.name: Acute viral laryngitis
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old elementary-school teacher who had a runny nose and sore throat 4 days ago, now with sudden hoarseness that has progressed to almost no voice. No stridor, no drooling, no breathing difficulty. T 37.3 C, RR 14, SpO2 99%; mildly red throat; neck supple.
correlates.workup: Laryngoscopy: red, swollen larynx and vocal folds, both moving normally; no mass.
correlates.management: Voice rest and a humidifier; antibiotics are rarely needed.

correlates.name: Adenocarcinoma in situ
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman who has never smoked and has no symptoms has a 2-cm faint, hazy peripheral nodule with no solid component, found on a CT done for kidney stones. SpO2 99%; spirometry normal.
correlates.workup: Wedge resection: tumor under 3 cm made entirely of dysplastic cells creeping along intact alveolar septa in a single scale-like layer, non-mucinous; no stromal, vascular or pleural invasion.
correlates.management: Complete resection is curative; preinvasive lesions do not inevitably progress. An invasive focus under 5 mm would reclassify it as microinvasive, still with a better prognosis than invasive disease.

correlates.name: Advanced CKD with volume overload and uremia
correlates.presentation: A 57-year-old man with diabetes, told at 50 his kidneys were mildly affected, stopped all his medicines. For 3 months: fatigue, poor appetite, nausea, itching, numb feet, swollen ankles, breathless on stairs, drowsy by noon. BP 168/96; scratch marks; leg edema; BUN 82 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: eGFR 25 mL/min, below 60 on every check for over 3 months; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 420 mg/g; BUN 82, creatinine 3.4 mg/dL; K+ 5.6, HCO3- 18, phosphate 6.1, calcium 7.9; Hgb 9.9 g/dL.
correlates.management: At GFR 15-29, prepare for kidney replacement with nephrology and the transplant team; at GFR below 15 start dialysis or transplant (preemptive or early transplant does best). Sodium under 2 g/day; ask about uremic symptoms at every visit.

correlates.name: Allergic asthma in a young adult
correlates.presentation: A 23-year-old woman with childhood eczema and spring hay fever has 6 months of episodic wheeze, chest tightness and dry cough that wake her at 3-4 a.m. and follow colds, time with her cat and hard laughing; she is well between bouts. End-expiratory wheeze; RR 20, SpO2 97%.
correlates.workup: FEV1/FVC 0.64, FEV1 71% predicted; 15 min after albuterol FEV1 rises 18% and 380 mL. DLCO 105%. Blood eosinophils 650/mm3, total IgE raised, skin prick tests positive to cat dander and house dust mite.
correlates.management: SABA for relief; daily inhaled corticosteroid plus LABA for maintenance. Check adherence and have her demonstrate the inhaler; rinse the mouth after the steroid; encase bedding, wash linens, remove carpets, limit the cat.

correlates.name: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
correlates.presentation: 26-year-old woman with asthma since childhood. Over 6 months, more wheeze and breathlessness despite high-dose inhaled steroids, and a cough bringing up thick brown mucus plugs. T 37.2 C, RR 20, SpO2 95%; wheezes in both lungs on breathing out.
correlates.workup: Eosinophils 1,400/uL; total IgE 2,800 IU/mL, with IgE specific for the mold's antigens. Coughed-up plugs contain branching septate hyphae; the mold sits in the airways without invading lung tissue.

correlates.name: Alport syndrome
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old boy whose grades improved after his teacher moved him to the front of the class; he often does not answer when spoken to. Maternal uncle started dialysis at 30. BP 112/70. UA many dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts and some protein.
correlates.workup: Audiogram: bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Biopsy: interstitial foam cells on trichrome; EM shows the lamina densa split and laminated into interwoven strands; IF nonspecific

correlates.name: Amantadine neurotoxicity
correlates.presentation: 80-year-old man with Parkinson disease on hemodialysis for ESRD takes a renally cleared antiparkinsonian drug at his usual dose; diphenhydramine was added for sleep. Over 1 day he is suddenly not making sense, agitated and hallucinating. T 36.8 C, no focal deficits
correlates.management: Stop the drug and the antihistamine and support him while it clears slowly (half-life about 8 days in ESRD; dialysis does not remove it). Sudden onset in an older patient: think drug, not age

correlates.name: Anemia of chronic kidney disease
correlates.presentation: A 62-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension and an eGFR of 34 for two years reports 4 months of tiredness and getting winded on one flight of stairs. No bleeding, no nausea or itching. BP 132/80, HR 92; pale conjunctivae; stool guaiac negative. Hgb 9.6 g/dL.
correlates.workup: Hgb 9.6 g/dL, MCV 88 fL, normal RDW, normal reticulocyte count; serum iron low, TIBC low, ferritin high. An erythropoietin level is sent only if the picture is confounding.

correlates.name: Angiomyolipoma
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old woman with no skin findings or family history: sudden severe right flank pain and lightheadedness. BP 88/56, HR 124. Hb 8.9 g/dL. CT: 9 cm right renal mass containing fat, with blood spreading around the kidney.
correlates.workup: Resected mass is yellow-tan; histology shows abnormal thick-walled blood vessels, sheets of smooth muscle and mature fat cells that look like large empty round spaces

correlates.name: Anterior pneumothorax in a supine patient
correlates.presentation: An intubated 45-year-old with several rib injuries after a fall can only be imaged lying flat in the trauma bay. BP 118/72, HR 104, SpO2 falling from 98% to 93% on FiO2 0.5; left chest slightly hyperresonant with softer breath sounds; trachea midline.
correlates.workup: Frontal film taken lying flat: no thin pleural line, but the left costophrenic angle runs far deeper and darker than the right, with extra lucency over the left lung base and upper abdomen and no lung markings between the left lower ribs.

correlates.name: Anthracosis
correlates.presentation: A 70-year-old office worker who has lived all his life in a large industrial city and smoked until 60 has no breathing complaints; FEV1/FVC 0.76, DLCO 90%. Black discoloration of the hilar nodes and the subpleural lung is noted at lobectomy for a peripheral nodule.
correlates.workup: Sections: black carbon pigment inside macrophages along the lymphatics, around bronchioles and in the hilar nodes, with no collagen nodules, no surrounding airspace enlargement and no interstitial scarring.

correlates.name: Anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome)
correlates.presentation: 28-year-old man with 3 weeks of worsening hemoptysis, dyspnea and chest pain; no fever, night sweats, sinus or nasal symptoms. Chest film: diffuse consolidations. UA dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts. Creatinine 1.1 rising to 3.9 mg/dL in 10 days.
correlates.workup: Serum IgG against the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen; ANCA negative. Biopsy: crescents in most glomeruli; smooth linear IgG and C3 along the GBM; no electron-dense deposits on EM
correlates.management: Urgent exchange plasmapheresis to strip out the circulating IgG and replace it with donor plasma

correlates.name: Asbestosis
correlates.presentation: A 72-year-old retired shipyard pipefitter (35 years, last worked 1992) who never smoked has 2 years of slowly worsening exertional dyspnea with little cough or sputum. Fine end-inspiratory crackles at both bases, clubbing; SpO2 91% at rest.
correlates.workup: TLC 63% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.86. Film: fine lace-like opacities starting in the lower zones, mid-zone parietal pleural plaques, no hilar nodes. Lavage: golden-brown rods with clubbed ends and a thin colorless core; biopsy: mixed-age scar.

correlates.name: Aspergilloma
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man who completed 6 months of four-drug treatment for a cavitating lung infection 15 years ago. Three months of coughing up a teaspoon of blood a few times a week; no fever or weight loss. T 36.9 C, RR 14, SpO2 96%; chest exam normal.
correlates.workup: Chest CT: round solid mass inside an old right upper lobe cavity; the mass shifts when he lies prone. Culture: septate hyphae branching at acute angles; spores in radiating chains.
correlates.management: Surgical resection of the cavity for repeated bleeding; voriconazole (or posaconazole, caspofungin, amphotericin B) if the mold starts invading tissue.

correlates.name: Aspiration pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 74-year-old man 2 months after a left-hemisphere stroke; coughs and chokes when he drinks, and vomited during an upper endoscopy 3 days ago. Now fever, tachypnea and cough with purulent sputum. T 38.7 C, HR 104, RR 26, SpO2 90%; coarse crackles and dullness at the right base.
correlates.workup: Chest film: right lower lobe infiltrate (the right main bronchus is steeper). Sputum culture: more than one organism, aerobes outnumbering anaerobes, mixed oral flora. Early chemical injury from gastric acid, then bacterial infection.
correlates.management: Blood and sputum cultures, then anaerobic coverage: clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, or metronidazole plus a beta-lactam. Prevent: speech and swallow evaluation, head of bed at 30-45 degrees, minimal sedation, oral care.

correlates.name: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old woman with adult-onset wheezing and a year of blocked nose and lost sense of smell develops severe wheeze, chest tightness and watery rhinorrhea 40 minutes after ibuprofen for a headache. Smooth, pale, glistening masses fill both nasal passages; SpO2 92%.
correlates.management: Avoid all NSAIDs and salicylates (COX-1 inhibition shunts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes); add a leukotriene receptor antagonist to her inhaled therapy.

correlates.name: Asthma with obesity
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old woman who never smoked, BMI 41, has occasional breathlessness and wheeze for 2 years with no workplace, allergy or drug triggers. Lungs clear today; SpO2 96%. FEV1/FVC 0.76, FEV1 72% predicted, TLC 98%; the flow-volume loop is hard to read.
correlates.workup: Methacholine challenge: FEV1 falls 41% from baseline after five breaths. Sputum and blood show little eosinophilic inflammation; total IgE normal.
correlates.management: Inhaled bronchodilator; whether weight loss improves control is not established.

correlates.name: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
correlates.presentation: A 79-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes in assisted living has a urine culture sent at a routine visit. She has no burning, frequency, fever, back pain or change in her thinking, and eats well. T 36.9 C, BP 132/78; abdomen and flanks nontender.
correlates.workup: Two clean-catch cultures on separate days each grow more than 100,000 CFU/mL of the same strain, with no symptoms to explain (a man needs one such culture; a catheter specimen counts above 100 CFU/mL).
correlates.management: No antibiotics: treating it in non-pregnant adults, older adults or diabetics is not indicated. The exception is a pregnant woman, who is screened and treated.

correlates.name: Atheroembolic renal disease
correlates.presentation: 74-year-old man with severe aortic atherosclerosis, 3 weeks after open repair of an abdominal aortic aneurysm without contrast: creatinine 1.1 rising to 2.9 mg/dL over 2 weeks. BP 162/94. No fever, no flank pain.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: interlobar arteries plugged by fibrosing material holding empty, needle-shaped clefts where cholesterol dissolved during tissue processing

correlates.name: Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and 40 pack-years of smoking: BP now 178/102 despite three drugs. Bruit over the left flank and upper abdomen. Creatinine 1.5 mg/dL. Ultrasound: left kidney 8.5 cm, right 11.5 cm.
correlates.workup: Plasma and left renal vein renin high; BP responds to an ACE inhibitor; arteriography localizes a plaque narrowing the left renal artery. Years untreated: shrunken left kidney, severe arteriolosclerosis on the right
correlates.management: BP drugs and risk-factor control, plus a stent or surgical removal of the narrowed segment when it drives the BP: unlike the idiopathic majority of high BP (over 90%), this renovascular cause can be fixed

correlates.name: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 24-year-old man with no diarrhea has his third episode in 4 years of pallor, fatigue and falling urine output; his brother needed dialysis. Afebrile, neuro exam normal. BP 168/100. Hb 8.0 g/dL, schistocytes, platelets 60,000/uL, creatinine 4.2 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Stool negative for Shiga toxin; ADAMTS13 activity not severely reduced; complement factor H deficient (or factor I / CD46 mutation). Biopsy: thick capillary walls with split, reduplicated GBM, concentric arteriolar thickening, scarring

correlates.name: Benign asbestos-related pleural plaques
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old retired insulation installer has no cough or dyspnea; a preoperative chest film shows calcified plates over both hemidiaphragm domes and the lateral chest walls. Lungs clear, SpO2 98%, FVC 96% predicted, DLCO 92%.
correlates.workup: CT: discrete, partly calcified plates on the parietal pleura and diaphragm; no lung scarring, effusion or mass. Autopsy: hard white patches of dense layered collagen with no coated fibres inside; number and size do not track the dose.
correlates.management: No treatment; they are harmless in themselves. Counsel that lung carcinoma, not a cancer of the chest lining, is the main cancer risk (about 5-fold, 55-fold with smoking), so never smoking matters most.

correlates.name: Benign nephrosclerosis
correlates.presentation: 71-year-old Black man with 20 years of high blood pressure; no symptoms. BP 148/88 on two drugs. Creatinine crept from 1.3 to 1.8 mg/dL over 5 years. UA trace protein, no blood or casts. Ultrasound: both kidneys small and symmetric.
correlates.workup: Nephrectomy or biopsy: finely granular cortical surface from subcapsular scars; arterioles with homogeneous pink hyaline walls and narrow lumens beside sclerosed glomeruli and atrophic tubules

correlates.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old man has 2 years of hesitancy, a weak stream, dribbling at the end, getting up 3 times a night, and sudden needs to void that sometimes leak before he reaches the toilet. Afebrile. Rectal exam: a smooth, symmetric, enlarged, rubbery, nontender gland.
correlates.workup: Urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 180 mL. Cystoscopy: the bladder wall is thickened, with coarse ridges of hypertrophied muscle bundles and a few small outpouchings.

correlates.name: Bladder exstrophy
correlates.presentation: Newborn boy: just below the tied umbilical cord a patch of moist, bright red mucosa lies open on the lower abdominal wall, and beneath it the penis is incompletely formed.
correlates.workup: Biopsy of the exposed mucosa later in life: glandular metaplasia; chronic infection that often climbs to the upper urinary tract

correlates.name: Blastomycosis
correlates.presentation: 48-year-old Wisconsin man who hunts and canoes, often digging along riverbanks. Two months of cough, fevers and a 6-kg weight loss, then raised crusted wart-like plaques on his face and shin and low back pain. T 38.1 C; tender L3 spinous process; lungs: crackles right upper zone.
correlates.workup: Sputum KOH prep: large thick-walled yeasts, each with a single broad-based bud. Skin biopsy: pus-filled granulomas (neutrophils inside granulomas). Spine film: lytic vertebral lesion. Serology is not useful.

correlates.name: Bronchial carcinoid tumor
correlates.presentation: A 50-year-old man who has never smoked has had a week of breathlessness with wheeze heard mainly on the right near the midline, and several watery stools a day with bouts of facial flushing; no weight loss. SpO2 95%. CT: a 3-cm mass projecting into the right main bronchus.
correlates.workup: Bronchoscopic biopsy: nests and ribbons of uniform cells with ample cytoplasm and finely stippled chromatin in a delicate fibrovascular stroma; fewer than 2 mitoses per 10 HPF and no necrosis; chromogranin and synaptophysin positive.
correlates.management: Surgical resection; the typical low-grade form generally behaves well. Only about 10% cause flushing and diarrhea.

correlates.name: Bronchiectasis
correlates.presentation: A 41-year-old woman who has never smoked, with sinus and ear infections since childhood, has coughed up a cupful of thick yellow-green sputum daily for 3 years, with repeated chest infections and two bouts of blood-streaked sputum. Clubbing; coarse basal crackles.
correlates.workup: CT: lower-lobe and lingular bronchi wider than their companion arteries that fail to taper toward the periphery, with thickened walls and mucus plugging; spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.66.
correlates.management: For a flare: send a new sputum culture and start empiric antibiotics tailored to the most recent culture, plus airway clearance, a mucoactive agent and oxygen; long-term goal of 2 or fewer exacerbations a year.

correlates.name: Calcium phosphate stones
correlates.presentation: A 28-year-old woman has passed a kidney stone every year or two since her teens. Serum HCO3- 17 with a normal anion gap and K+ 3.1, yet her urine pH is 6.9. Plain film: a radiopaque stone plus fine stippled densities scattered through the inner zones of both kidneys.
correlates.workup: Urine pH 7.0; wedge-shaped prism crystals in the sediment; non-contrast CT: a dense white stone and deposits throughout the renal medullas of both kidneys.
correlates.management: Low-sodium diet and a thiazide, plus citrate, which complexes Ca2+ in the urine and lowers its saturation.

correlates.name: Candidemia (invasive candidiasis)
correlates.presentation: 61-year-old man in the surgical ICU 12 days after a bowel resection, with a central venous catheter, parenteral nutrition, 10 days of broad-spectrum antibiotics and steroids. Fever persists despite the antibiotics. T 39.0 C, HR 120, BP 88/50; new white lesions on the retina.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures: budding yeasts with pseudohyphae; germ tubes form at 37 C. Bacterial cultures negative.
correlates.management: Disseminated disease: amphotericin B with an azole, or caspofungin (an echinocandin); check susceptibilities, because fluconazole overuse has bred resistant species.

correlates.name: Candiduria
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes has been in the ICU for 12 days with a Foley and is on a third broad-spectrum antibiotic. A surveillance urine culture is sent. No fever or flank pain; vitals stable. Dipstick: trace leukocyte esterase, nitrite negative.
correlates.workup: Urine microscopy: budding yeast cells and elongated chains of cells that fail to separate; the isolate forms germ tubes when incubated at 37 C.

correlates.name: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema
correlates.presentation: A 72-year-old man with a prior heart attack (EF 30%) has 3 days of worsening breathlessness, needing 3 pillows, waking up gasping, and a 4-kg weight gain. BP 168/96, HR 108, RR 28, SpO2 86%; crackles to mid-lung on both sides, JVP 14 cm, an S3, ankle swelling.
correlates.workup: Film: enlarged heart; white airspace opacity fanning out from both hila with the apices and the lung bases relatively spared; lung markings crowd the outer third of both lungs.
correlates.management: IV loop diuretic (furosemide); the repeat film shows the opacities largely resolved, with some residue.

correlates.name: Catheter-associated UTI
correlates.presentation: A 71-year-old man has had an indwelling Foley since hip surgery 9 days ago. Today he has T 38.6 C, new confusion and lower abdominal discomfort; the drainage bag holds cloudy, foul-smelling urine. He reports no burning. HR 104, BP 122/70.
correlates.workup: Urine drawn through a freshly replaced Foley: pyuria and more than 100,000 CFU/mL of a gram-negative rod; the removed tube's lumen is crusted and narrowed by biofilm.

correlates.name: Cauda equina syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old warehouse worker has had 2 days of low back pain after lifting; today shooting pain and weakness in both legs, numbness of the buttocks, perineum and inner thighs, and he has leaked urine and stool without noticing. Ankle jerks absent bilaterally.
correlates.management: A medical and surgical emergency: recognize it early and arrange emergent spine imaging and surgical decompression the same day; delay risks permanent leg, bladder and bowel deficits.

correlates.name: Central airway tumor mimicking asthma
correlates.presentation: A previously healthy 10-year-old girl has 9 months of episodic wheeze, dyspnea and steadily worsening tolerance for running, unchanged by albuterol, inhaled steroids, montelukast and two bursts of oral prednisone. No eczema or allergies; afebrile, SpO2 97%, expiratory wheeze.
correlates.workup: Flow-volume loop: the expiratory limb is cut off into a flat plateau while the inspiratory limb is normal; no bronchodilator response. CT: a polypoid mass inside the lower trachea.
correlates.management: Remove the lesion; the flow-volume loop returns to normal. Lesson: when correct therapy fails, question the diagnosis instead of adding drugs.

correlates.name: Central sleep apnea
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old man had a brainstem stroke 3 months ago and has slurred speech. His wife sees long pauses at night in which his chest and belly do not move at all before he breathes again; he wakes unrefreshed. BMI 24, throat not crowded; awake SpO2 96%.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: repeated 15-25 s pauses in nasal and oral airflow with the chest and abdominal belts flat (no effort), each with SpO2 falling to 87%; no runs of deep, fast breaths before the pauses.
correlates.management: Treat the underlying neurologic cause; give oxygen as needed. CPAP or BiPAP helps only about 1 in 5, because the airway is open and the drive to breathe is what is missing.

correlates.name: Cheyne-Stokes breathing
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with end-stage ischemic heart failure, EF 12%, waits in the hospital at the top of the transplant list. At night nurses see cycles: his breaths become rapid and deep, then stop altogether with no chest movement, then the cycle repeats. BP 92/60.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: runs of rapid, deep breaths alternating with pauses in which airflow and chest and abdominal effort both stop; SpO2 dips in each pause and CO2 swings low after each run.
correlates.management: Treat the failing heart, the underlying cause (here, transplant); oxygen as needed. CPAP or BiPAP adds little: slow circulation delays the brain's feedback, so the airway is not the problem.

correlates.name: Cholera
correlates.presentation: Relief worker, 34, in a post-earthquake camp drinking untreated river water. Since yesterday: sudden painless, profuse watery diarrhea, pale gray with mucus flecks; no fever, no blood. T 36.9 C, HR 128, BP 78/44; sunken eyes, skin tenting.
correlates.workup: Stool: no white cells or blood; curved, oxidase-positive gram-negative rods grow on thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar. K+ 2.8 mEq/L, HCO3- 14 mEq/L, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL.
correlates.management: Oral rehydration with electrolyte replacement - very treatable this way, against 25-50% mortality untreated. Reportable to the CDC.

correlates.name: Chronic bacterial prostatitis
correlates.presentation: A 48-year-old man has had 5 months of on-and-off aching in the perineum and pelvis with mild burning and frequency; two 1-week antibiotic courses helped only briefly. Afebrile, vitals normal. Rectal exam: gland mildly tender, not boggy; no urethral discharge.
correlates.workup: Urine more than 10 WBC per high-power field, yet the voided culture grows few or no bacteria (about 70% are 'sterile'); expressed prostatic secretions can grow the organism.
correlates.management: Still culture the urine and treat empirically at first; if there is pyuria without bacteria, test for chlamydia.

correlates.name: Chronic beryllium disease
correlates.presentation: A 56-year-old machinist who has cut and ground metal parts for aerospace and nuclear-weapons contractors for 20 years has 8 months of dry cough, dyspnea, chest pain, 5-kg weight loss, fatigue and joint aches. Few crackles; SpO2 93%; FVC 71% predicted.
correlates.workup: CT: ill-defined upper-lobe nodular and irregular opacities with mildly enlarged hilar nodes. Biopsy: noncaseating epithelioid granulomas with helper T-cell alveolitis. Lavage lymphocytes proliferate when cultured with the workplace metal.

correlates.name: Chronic bronchitis
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old man with 45 pack-years has coughed up sputum on most days for 4-5 months of every year for the past 3 years, with exertional dyspnea. BMI 33, cyanotic lips, scattered wheezes and coarse crackles, ankle edema. SpO2 87%; hematocrit 56%.
correlates.workup: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.60, FEV1 55% predicted, no meaningful bronchodilator response. Airway biopsy: enlarged, multiplied submucosal mucous glands filling more than half the wall between epithelium and cartilage.

correlates.name: Chronic cough from an ACE inhibitor
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old man has a dry, tickling cough for 3 months that began 5 weeks after lisinopril was started for hypertension; no heartburn, nasal drainage, wheeze or sputum. Lungs clear; chest film and spirometry normal.
correlates.management: Review the medication list and stop the offending antihypertensive; the cough fades over the following weeks.

correlates.name: Chronic cough from gastroesophageal reflux
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman has 4 months of dry cough, worse after large evening meals and when lying flat, with burning retrosternal discomfort and a sour taste in her mouth; no nasal symptoms, wheeze or new drugs. Lungs clear; chest film and spirometry normal.
correlates.management: Treat the acid aggressively (acid suppression); the cough, and any coexisting asthma, often improves.

correlates.name: Chronic cough from postnasal drip
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man has 3 months of persistent cough with constant throat clearing and a sense of mucus running down the back of his throat, plus nasal congestion and recurring facial pressure; no heartburn, wheeze or new drugs. Afebrile; chest film and spirometry normal.

correlates.name: Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old woman has 3 months of cough, low-grade fevers, drenching night sweats, 6-kg weight loss and exertional dyspnea, never in respiratory failure. SpO2 94%. WBC 11,800 with eosinophils 1,400/mm3. Chest film: dense opacities confined to the outer lung zones.
correlates.workup: BAL eosinophils 52% of cells, mycobacterial and fungal cultures negative; parasite serology negative. Biopsy: focal consolidation with lymphocytes and eosinophils in the septal walls and alveoli.
correlates.management: Oral corticosteroids, to which it responds; follow for later scarring of the lung.

correlates.name: Chronic gouty nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man with 25 years of attacks of a hot, swollen big toe and chalky lumps over both elbows; now gets up twice a night to urinate. BP 146/90. Creatinine 1.4 rising to 2.2 mg/dL over 4 years. UA no blood, trace protein.
correlates.workup: Biopsy, medulla: needle-shaped birefringent monosodium urate crystals in distal tubules, collecting ducts and interstitium, ringed by elongated macrophages and foreign-body giant cells; cortical atrophy and scarring

correlates.name: Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old with painless white plaques coating the tongue and cheeks on and off since infancy, thick crumbling fingernails and red scaly patches in the skin folds, each returning after every topical course. T 36.8 C; growth normal; never had a bloodstream or deep infection.
correlates.workup: Scrapings: budding yeasts with pseudohyphae. HIV test negative. Genetic testing: mutation disrupting IL-17 signaling.
correlates.management: Topical nystatin or an azole for the mouth and skin, oral azoles for the nails; expect recurrences, since the IL-17 defect persists.

correlates.name: Chronic pyelonephritis
correlates.presentation: 30-year-old woman, urinary infections since childhood, when a voiding study showed urine rising from the bladder up both ureters. Now asymptomatic; BP 152/96; creatinine 1.0 to 1.7 mg/dL in 3 years. UA 1+ protein, few WBCs, broad casts. Ultrasound: small, scarred right kidney.
correlates.workup: Imaging: asymmetric kidneys with coarse U-shaped cortical scars over blunted, dilated, deformed calyces. Histology: lymphocytes and monocytes in the interstitium; dilated tubules filled with homogeneous eosinophilic casts

correlates.name: Chronic respiratory acidosis in COPD
correlates.presentation: A 77-year-old man who smoked 2 packs a day for 50 years and uses three inhalers had a clinic ABG on room air: pH 7.35, PaCO2 65, HCO3- 33. Today paramedics put him on 15 L/min oxygen for a chest cold; within an hour he is drowsy, RR 8, SpO2 99%.
correlates.management: Give only a little oxygen, titrated low, if needed: high-flow oxygen can push his CO2 higher and stop his breathing. Avoid sedatives; use CPAP or BiPAP by mask, or intubate, if ventilation stays poor.

correlates.name: Chronic silicosis
correlates.presentation: A 60-year-old stonemason who has cut and dressed quarry granite for 28 years has a year of chronic cough, worsening exertional dyspnea, fatigue and mild weight loss; afebrile. Few crackles; SpO2 93%. FVC 72% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.74, DLCO 61%.
correlates.workup: Film: small rounded upper-zone nodules; thin rims of calcium around the hilar nodes. Biopsy: nodules of concentric, whorled hyalinized collagen ringed by dust-laden macrophages; weakly birefringent particles on polarization; no granulomas.

correlates.name: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man, 40 pack-years: painless visible hematuria and dull left flank pain, with 4 kg weight loss. New left scrotal varicocele. BP 150/92. Hb 18.9 g/dL, calcium 9.4 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: CT: upper-pole mass with tumor growing into the left renal vein and IVC. Gross: bright yellow with hemorrhage, necrosis, cysts. Histology: polygonal cells with empty-looking cytoplasm (glycogen, lipid) in a delicate branching capillary net
correlates.management: Partial or radical nephrectomy, chosen by tumor size and comorbidities

correlates.name: Clostridioides difficile colitis
correlates.presentation: 79-year-old woman, hospital day 9, on a broad-spectrum antibiotic for pneumonia. Three days of 8-10 watery, non-bloody stools a day. T 38.3 C, HR 106, BP 108/64; abdomen mildly distended and diffusely tender.
correlates.workup: Stool PCR or antigen test for toxins A and B positive within hours (culture needs anaerobic media and days). Colonoscopy: a membrane-like coat of plaques over inflamed colonic mucosa.
correlates.management: Contact and enteric precautions; wash hands with soap and water (alcohol gel does not kill spores). Oral fidaxomicin or oral vancomycin first-line, metronidazole second-line; surgery for toxic megacolon; fecal transplant for recurrences.

correlates.name: Collapsing FSGS
correlates.presentation: 31-year-old Black man off antiretroviral therapy for 2 years (CD4 90/uL): 3 weeks of fast-worsening leg and scrotal swelling and frothy urine. UA 4+ protein, 24-h protein 14 g. Creatinine 1.2 rising to 3.4 mg/dL over 6 weeks.
correlates.workup: Biopsy, PAS: glomerular tufts shrunken and retracted with closed capillary loops, capped by enlarged, crowded podocytes and parietal epithelial cells

correlates.name: Common cold
correlates.presentation: 26-year-old father of two toddlers in daycare, in October. Two days of sneezing, clear runny nose, blocked nose, mild sore throat, headache and dry cough. T 37.0 C, HR 76, SpO2 99%; clear nasal discharge, mildly red throat without exudate or nodes; lungs clear.
correlates.management: Over-the-counter symptom relief (fluids, rest, decongestant); no antibiotics and no specific antiviral; resolves in 5-7 days in adults, about 10 in children.

correlates.name: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old woman with diabetes and an eGFR of 34, taking metformin, ibuprofen and chlorthalidone, has an abdominal CT with IV iodinated dye for pain. Two days later her creatinine is 2.5 mg/dL (1.6 before) and her urine output has fallen. BP never below 120/70; no rash.
correlates.management: Before any iodinated study in CKD: hold metformin the day before (lactic acidosis risk) and restart after; stop NSAIDs 2 days and loop or thiazide-type diuretics 24 hours before; holding ACEi/ARB is debated. Use MRI if the dye is a problem.

correlates.name: Cor pulmonale from advanced restrictive disease
correlates.presentation: A 69-year-old man with 4 years of progressive lung scarring (FVC 48%, DLCO 30%) has 2 months of ankle swelling and fatigue. JVP 12 cm, rising further with 15 s of pressure over the liver at 45 degrees; left parasternal lift; right-sided gallop; pitting edema to the knees.

correlates.name: COVID-19 at high risk of progression (outpatient)
correlates.presentation: 68-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Scratchy throat, headache and muscle aches since yesterday, slowly getting worse; positive home antigen test this morning. T 37.9 C, HR 92, RR 16, SpO2 97% on room air; lungs clear.
correlates.management: Review his drug list for CYP3A4 interactions (boxed warning), then nirmatrelvir with ritonavir every 12 h for 5 days, started within 5 days of onset; adjust for renal function. Alternatives: 3 days of IV remdesivir, or molnupiravir.

correlates.name: COVID-19 rebound
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old woman with diabetes finished 5 days of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir, felt well and had a negative home antigen test on day 6. On day 9 her sore throat and nasal congestion return, mildly. T 37.4 C, HR 80, RR 14, SpO2 98%; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: Home antigen test positive again, within 10 days of the negative test that followed the full course.
correlates.management: Reassure and give supportive care: recurrent symptoms are usually mild, and a second course of nirmatrelvir-ritonavir is not routinely recommended.

correlates.name: Croup (laryngotracheobronchitis)
correlates.presentation: 2-year-old at daycare in November with 2 days of runny nose and low-grade temperature, then a harsh repetitive cough and hoarse voice, worse at night. T 38.3 C, HR 120, RR 30, SpO2 96%; agitated, high-pitched noise on breathing in; no drooling; sits comfortably.
correlates.workup: Diagnosis is clinical. Frontal soft-tissue neck film (abnormal in 40-50%): the subglottic trachea narrows and tapers upward instead of having square shoulders; supraglottic tissues normal on the lateral view. Nasal PCR if needed.

correlates.name: Cryptococcal meningitis in HIV
correlates.presentation: 36-year-old man with untreated HIV who keeps racing pigeons. Three weeks of worsening headache and fever, now vomiting and confusion. T 38.3 C, HR 100, BP 132/84; disoriented, mild neck stiffness; a few umbilicated papules on the face.
correlates.workup: CD4 35/uL. CSF: budding yeasts with narrow-based buds and a wide clear capsule on negative stain; capsular antigen positive by latex agglutination in CSF and blood; CSF culture grows the yeast.
correlates.management: Amphotericin B plus flucytosine first, then long-term fluconazole.

correlates.name: Cryptorchidism
correlates.presentation: A 6-month-old boy born at 34 weeks has a flat, small, empty right hemiscrotum. A soft fullness in the right groin, which his parents call a hernia, cannot be massaged down into the scrotum. The left side is normal; the penis is normal.
correlates.management: Observe to 9-12 months if it may still descend (refer early if very high); urology by 12 months to bring it down and tack it in place; an intra-abdominal testis is removed. Cancer and subfertility risk persist - lifelong self-exams.

correlates.name: Cystinuria
correlates.presentation: A 15-year-old boy is seen in clinic after passing his third kidney stone since age 11; his older sister has also formed stones, and neither parent has. Growth, BP and exam are normal; serum calcium and creatinine normal.
correlates.workup: Urine sodium cyanide-nitroprusside test positive; flat six-sided crystals in the sediment; urine also wastes ornithine, lysine and arginine. The stone is only faintly radiopaque on plain film, moderately dense on CT.
correlates.management: Low-sodium diet, alkalinize the urine, and add a chelating agent that binds the lost amino acid and helps dissolve the stone.

correlates.name: Dengue
correlates.presentation: 27-year-old back 5 days from a month in the Philippines, many mosquito bites. Sudden high fever, chills, malaise, severe headache, pain behind the eyes and intense pain in the back, joints, muscles and bones; a red rash. T 39.8 C, HR 104, BP 118/72.
correlates.management: Supportive only: there is no antiviral. Watch for the severe hemorrhagic form with shock and kidney failure, mainly on reinfection with a different serotype (15% mortality untreated, about 1% with supportive care).

correlates.name: Dense deposit disease (MPGN type II)
correlates.presentation: 13-year-old girl with no recent sore throat or skin infection: 3 weeks of dark, frothy urine and a puffy face. BP 148/94. UA RBCs, RBC casts, 3 g/day protein. Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL. C3 low, C4 normal, ASO negative; C3 still low 4 months later.
correlates.workup: Low C3, factor B and properdin with normal C1 and C4; C3 nephritic factor in serum. Biopsy: GBM doubled on silver stain; only C3 and properdin on IF; a ribbon of electron-opaque material inside the GBM

correlates.name: Desquamative interstitial pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old man who smokes 1.5 packs a day has 4 months of slowly increasing dyspnea and a dry cough. Fine basal crackles and early clubbing. FVC 76% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.82, DLCO 50%.
correlates.workup: Lung biopsy: alveolar airspaces uniformly packed with brown-pigmented macrophages whose cytoplasm holds lamellar bodies (surfactant debris from dead type II pneumocytes); alveolar walls only mildly thickened.
correlates.management: Stop smoking and start systemic corticosteroids; the response is excellent, though a few go on to scarring.

correlates.name: Diabetic nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for 25 years who stopped seeing doctors: weight gain, swelling to the thighs and worsening vision. BP 158/92, HbA1c 10.4%. UA heavy protein, slight blood. Albumin 2.1 g/dL, lipids high, PT/INR normal.
correlates.workup: Urine albumin first rose into the microalbumin range, then became heavy proteinuria. Biopsy: round PAS- and trichrome-positive mesangial nodules, glassy hyaline arteriolar walls, thick GBM; nonspecific IF
avoid: Advanced CKD with volume overload and uremia

correlates.name: Diphtheria
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old who never received childhood vaccines, with 2 days of sore throat and low fever. T 38.2 C, HR 116. At first look the throat is red with no exudate; minutes later a small gray-white patch on one tonsil is visibly spreading across the oropharynx within 10-15 minutes.
correlates.management: Treat as an emergency at once, without waiting for tests, and protect the airway; a macrolide such as erythromycin is active. Prevented by DTaP and Tdap.

correlates.name: Disseminated coccidioidomycosis
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old Filipino woman, 33 weeks pregnant, living in Tucson. Two months of fever, cough and weight loss, then enlarging ulcerated skin nodules on the face, a hot swollen ankle and a week of headache. T 38.7 C, HR 108; tender left ankle effusion; mild neck stiffness.
correlates.workup: Skin biopsy: granulomas containing thick-walled spherules full of endospores. Complement fixation IgG titer high. Ankle film: lytic bone lesion. Culture deliberately avoided.
correlates.management: IV amphotericin B for disseminated disease; fluconazole when the meninges are involved, though results there are relatively poor.

correlates.name: Disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex in HIV
correlates.presentation: 39-year-old man with HIV who stopped his antiretrovirals a year ago. Five weeks of fevers, drenching night sweats and a 7-kg weight loss; no cough or breathlessness. T 38.8 C, HR 104, RR 16, SpO2 98%; thin; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: CD4 count 32/uL; Hb 8.6 g/dL; alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L with normal bilirubin; chest film clear.
correlates.management: Azithromycin (or clarithromycin) plus ethambutol, with vision checks; add rifabutin as a third drug if sicker, since it spares the antiretrovirals the induction rifampin causes. Azithromycin prophylaxis once CD4 < 50.

correlates.name: Ebola / Marburg virus disease
correlates.presentation: 36-year-old nurse back 8 days from treating patients in an outbreak in Uganda. Headache, fever, sore throat and muscle aches, then abdominal pain, vomiting, watery diarrhea and a rash; now oozing blood from IV sites and gums. T 39.8 C, HR 124, BP 84/52.
correlates.workup: ELISA and RT-PCR of blood positive, run with special precautions in a high-containment lab; high viral titers in most tissues.
correlates.management: Strict isolation (spread is by blood and body fluids). Supportive: IV fluids, electrolytes, oxygen, pressure support, antiemetics, fever and pain control, treat other infections; antibodies protect (monoclonals REGN-EB3, mAb114).

correlates.name: Emphysema-predominant COPD
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old woman with 50 pack-years has 3 years of progressive exertional dyspnea, little cough or sputum and 8-kg weight loss. Thin, breathes out slowly through pursed lips, uses neck muscles; quiet breath sounds, prolonged expiration. SpO2 93%; PaCO2 38 mmHg.
correlates.workup: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.52, FEV1 45% predicted, TLC 125%, RV 180%, DLCO 40%. Film: flattened diaphragms, widened rib spaces, hyperlucent lungs, long narrow heart; CT: upper-lobe loss of tissue around the central acinus.
correlates.management: Stop smoking; one long-acting bronchodilator (LABA or LAMA), or LABA plus LAMA if symptoms are high or exacerbations frequent; SABA or SAMA for rescue; long-term oxygen if hypoxemic, the only step proven to improve survival.

correlates.name: Empyema
correlates.presentation: 70-year-old man on day 10 of antibiotics for right lower lobe pneumonia, still spiking fevers to 39.2 C with right-sided pain on breathing in and a 3-kg weight loss. HR 106, RR 24, SpO2 93%; dullness, absent breath sounds and reduced fremitus over the right lower chest.
correlates.workup: Chest film: right pleural collection with a straight horizontal air-fluid line reaching the chest wall. Thoracentesis: thick, opaque pus full of neutrophils, with bacteria on Gram stain.

correlates.name: Enteric hyperoxaluria (Crohn disease)
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old woman had 60 cm of terminal ileum resected for transmural inflammatory bowel disease with fistulas. She has 4-6 loose, greasy, foul-smelling stools a day and comes to clinic after passing her second kidney stone this year. BMI 18; afebrile.
correlates.workup: 24-hour urine: oxalate 78 mg/day (high), calcium normal; sediment shows small square crystals with an X across them; the stone is radiopaque on plain film.
correlates.management: Do not restrict dietary calcium - eaten with meals it binds oxalate in the gut, and a low-calcium diet frees more oxalate for absorption. Low-sodium diet; thiazide for recurrent calcium stones.

correlates.name: Epiglottitis
correlates.presentation: 4-year-old, arrived from abroad last month, never vaccinated. Six hours of high fever and severe sore throat; now drooling, refusing to swallow, sitting upright with the head pushed forward. T 39.8 C, HR 150, RR 32, SpO2 93%; muffled voice, soft inspiratory stridor; little cough.
correlates.workup: Lateral neck film: a rounded supraglottic soft-tissue swelling filling the air space above the larynx. Blood culture: gram-negative coccobacilli that grow on chocolate agar (need factors V and X).
correlates.management: Secure the airway at once, usually by endotracheal intubation, before anything that might upset the child; then IV ampicillin-sulbactam, cefuroxime or ceftriaxone (TMP-SMX if penicillin-allergic). Prevented by the type b conjugate vaccine.

correlates.name: Ethylene glycol poisoning
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man is found drowsy in his garage 8 hours after drinking from a jug of automotive coolant after a fight with his wife. He breathes fast and deep, RR 32, BP 130/80. Vision is normal. Na+ 140, Cl- 101, HCO3- 7; pH 7.10, PaCO2 20.
correlates.workup: Creatinine climbs from 1.0 to 4.2 mg/dL over 2 days. Kidney biopsy: tubular cells swollen and ballooned; under polarized light, calcium oxalate crystals sit in and plug the tubular lumens.
correlates.management: Fomepizole to block alcohol dehydrogenase; add thiamine and pyridoxine, cofactors that speed the toxin's harmless breakdown; saline diuresis; IV or oral ethanol if no fomepizole; dialysis if severe.

correlates.name: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
correlates.presentation: A 17-year-old cross-country runner with no symptoms at rest or at night gets cough, chest tightness and wheeze that start about 10 minutes into winter races in cold, dry air and peak at 20-30 minutes. Exam and resting spirometry normal (FEV1/FVC 0.84).
correlates.workup: Treadmill challenge raising the heart rate to 80% of maximum for 6 minutes, then FEV1 every 5 minutes for 30 minutes: FEV1 falls 19% from baseline. Resting spirometry and lung volumes normal.
correlates.management: Longer warm-up, a mask to warm the inspired air, and an inhaled beta-2 agonist before activity (prevents over 80% of episodes); the goal is no limit on any sport. Ask whether the underlying disease is poorly controlled.

correlates.name: Febrile UTI (pyelonephritis) in an infant
correlates.presentation: A 9-month-old girl has 2 days of T 39.6 C, vomiting, loose stools, poor feeding and fussiness; her parents thought it was a stomach bug. Prenatal scans were normal. She is now lethargic: HR 172, RR 40, capillary refill 3 s. No cough, ear findings or rash.
correlates.workup: Catheterized urine: pyuria and a culture growing a gram-negative rod within a day (a bag specimen is for screening urinalysis only). Renal ultrasound after treatment: normal.
correlates.management: Culture a catheterized specimen, never a bag; then IV or IM ceftriaxone or cefotaxime (ampicillin plus gentamicin in neonates) with IV fluids for a day or two. Renal ultrasound for every infant; full workup after a second infection.

correlates.name: Fibromuscular dysplasia
correlates.presentation: 27-year-old woman who smokes: BP 172/108 at a clinic visit, confirmed twice and not controlled on two drugs; no family history of high BP, no diabetes. Bruit over the right upper abdomen. Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: High plasma renin; arteriography shows a narrowed renal artery. Artery wall on elastic stain: media markedly thickened by smooth muscle hyperplasia, elastic lamina disrupted, lumen narrowed

correlates.name: Fixed upper-airway obstruction (tracheal or subglottic stenosis)
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old woman who never smoked has 5 years of slowly worsening exertional dyspnea and noisy breathing heard on both inhaling and exhaling; inhalers have not helped. Lungs clear; SpO2 97%. FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 47% predicted.
correlates.workup: Flow-volume loop: both the expiratory and the inspiratory limbs are cut off into flat plateaus; the expiratory curve alone looked like ordinary obstruction. Bronchoscopy: concentric narrowing just below the vocal cords.
correlates.management: Stent or surgically repair the narrowed segment, which improves function markedly; treat a driving cause such as ANCA-associated vasculitis.

correlates.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old Black man, homeless, injects heroin: 2 months of frothy urine and leg swelling. BP 162/98. UA 4+ protein, small blood, few WBCs. Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, albumin 2.2 g/dL, 24-h protein 7 g. HIV test negative.
correlates.workup: Non-selective proteinuria. Biopsy: in only some glomeruli, part of the tuft is scarred with glassy hyaline deposits; IF negative except IgM and C3 in the scars; EM shows effacement without deposits

correlates.name: Functional incontinence
correlates.presentation: An 84-year-old man with severe hip arthritis who walks slowly with a walker, recently started on a nightly sleeping pill, wets himself on the way to the bathroom, mostly at night. He knows when he needs to go. Urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 50 mL.
correlates.management: Treat the underlying cause - delirium, infection, atrophic vaginitis, pharmacologic agents, psychiatric illness, endocrine disease, reduced mobility or dexterity, stool impaction: here stop the sedative and address his mobility.

correlates.name: Genitourinary tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old man treated years ago in his home country for a cough with night sweats (he stopped the pills early) has 4 months of frequency, burning and a dull right flank ache that two antibiotic courses did not touch. Afebrile; mild right flank tenderness.
correlates.workup: Urine: white and red cells. An acid-fast stain of a spun urine sample shows slender red-staining rods.

correlates.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old woman with 4 months of recurrent sinusitis, bloody nasal crusts and nosebleeds, now coughing blood. Perforated nasal septum. BP 150/92. UA RBC casts, 1+ protein. Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL. No asthma; eosinophils normal.
correlates.workup: PR3 (cytoplasmic-pattern) ANCA positive; IgG to GBM collagen negative. Biopsy: crescents with necrotizing small-vessel inflammation; little or no immunoglobulin or complement on IF; wrinkled, ruptured GBM on EM

correlates.name: Hair tourniquet syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 4-month-old has cried inconsolably for 6 hours and is feeding poorly. Afebrile, HR 168, otherwise well-appearing; ears, abdomen and diaper area normal. With the socks off, the left second toe is swollen and red-purple beyond a thin, deep groove encircling its base.
correlates.management: A vascular emergency: cut the constricting strand off at once, through the groove, before the digit dies (sedation, or the ED, if it is wrapped around the penis). In any inconsolable infant, look in the diaper and under the socks.

correlates.name: Hand-foot-mouth disease
correlates.presentation: 3-year-old at daycare in late August; two classmates are ill too. Two days of low fever, refusing food as swallowing hurts. T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 128; painful oral ulcers; non-itchy red spots and small blisters on the palms and soles.
correlates.management: Supportive: fluids and analgesia for painful swallowing; self-limited over 7-10 days. The virus keeps shedding in stool for up to 6 weeks (throat up to 4), so stress hygiene at daycare.

correlates.name: Hansen disease (leprosy)
correlates.presentation: 50-year-old man with slowly evolving skin lesions on the face, trunk and right arm, first noticed after a stay in South America. BP 145/90. Widespread skin nodules and scaly plaques, thickened skin on the cheeks and feet, skin ulcers, marked muscle weakness.
correlates.management: Dapsone (check G6PD; avoid with sulfa allergy) with rifampin and clofazimine (pink skin, QT; from a national program). Thalidomide for a severe painful nodular inflammatory reaction: pregnancy tests and two forms of birth control.

correlates.name: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
correlates.presentation: 41-year-old man in rural New Mexico who swept out a shut-up cabin full of mouse droppings 2 weeks ago. Four days of fever, headache and muscle aches, then rapidly worsening breathlessness. T 38.9 C, HR 122, BP 86/50, RR 34, SpO2 82%; crackles throughout; no bleeding.
correlates.workup: Chest film: bilateral pulmonary edema with a normal-sized heart. Four-fold rise in IgG between acute and convalescent sera; RT-PCR positive.
correlates.management: Supportive care, usually in the ICU (oxygen, ventilatory support); up to 30% die. Caught by inhaling dust from deer mouse urine and droppings.

correlates.name: Herpangina
correlates.presentation: 4-year-old at a summer day camp with 1 day of fever and a sore throat; drinks little as swallowing hurts. T 39.4 C, HR 132; a dozen painful sores at the back of the mouth and throat only; gums, lips, palms and soles normal.

correlates.name: Hiatal hernia
correlates.presentation: A 74-year-old woman with fullness after meals has a routine chest film before cataract surgery that shows a round gas-containing structure projecting over the heart. Afebrile, no cough or sputum, WBC 7,200/mm3, lungs clear on exam.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: inside the round structure over the heart, gas sits above a straight horizontal fluid level with debris; the lateral film places it behind the heart, continuous with the upper abdomen; lungs clear.

correlates.name: Histoplasmosis
correlates.presentation: 24-year-old college student from Kentucky, 12 days after a weekend exploring caves full of roosting bats; three friends on the trip are ill too. Fever, dry cough, chest ache and fatigue. T 38.4 C, HR 98, RR 20, SpO2 95%; lungs clear; liver and spleen not felt.
correlates.workup: Chest CT: several small nodules in both lungs. Antigen positive in urine and blood by enzyme immunoassay. Biopsy: tiny oval yeasts packed inside macrophages; later these foci calcify (dormant organisms can reactivate).
correlates.management: Itraconazole for mild or moderate disease (most heavy exposures settle on their own); amphotericin B for severe lung disease or dissemination, as in AIDS.

correlates.name: Hospital-acquired pneumonia, not ventilated
correlates.presentation: 55-year-old woman with COPD who had IV antibiotics for a UTI 6 weeks ago, admitted for a COPD flare and never intubated. At 56 hours: new fever, purulent sputum and falling saturation. T 38.9 C, HR 110, RR 28, BP 86/52, SpO2 86%; crackles and dullness at the right base.
correlates.workup: Admission film clear; now a new right lower lobe infiltrate. WBC 17,800/uL, mostly neutrophils. Sputum Gram stain: gram-negative rods plus gram-positive cocci in clusters. Blood and sputum cultures taken before antibiotics.
correlates.management: Cultures, then broad empiric cover at once because IV antibiotics within 90 days raise multidrug-resistance risk: vancomycin plus imipenem plus an aminoglycoside in shock; narrow as soon as cultures and the patient allow.

correlates.name: Hospitalized COVID-19, not mechanically ventilated
correlates.presentation: 77-year-old man admitted after 4 days of fever, dry cough and increasing breathlessness following a positive home antigen test. T 38.4 C, HR 104, RR 24, SpO2 89% on room air, 94% on 2 L by nasal cannula; crackles at both bases; alert, not intubated.
correlates.management: IV remdesivir once daily, usually for 5 days, in a unit that can treat anaphylaxis; watch for bradycardia and rising aminotransferases; hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine can blunt its effect.

correlates.name: Hyperkalemia in CKD
correlates.presentation: A 70-year-old man with stage 3b kidney disease (eGFR 38) and heart failure started lisinopril 3 weeks ago; since then he takes ibuprofen daily for knee pain and drinks orange juice each morning. His legs feel weak. HR 52, BP 124/70; K+ 6.6 mEq/L, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (his usual).
correlates.management: Find the cause: stop the NSAID and cut dietary potassium; the ACE inhibitor may not need to stop if something else is responsible. Recheck electrolytes 2-4 weeks after any ACE inhibitor/ARB change. IV bicarbonate shifts K+ into cells.

correlates.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old dairy farmer has had repeated bouts of fever, chills, dry cough and breathlessness that start 4-6 hours after forking stored damp hay and settle within a day away from the barn. Today T 38.4 C, RR 24, SpO2 90%, fine crackles at both bases.
correlates.workup: Serum precipitating IgG against the barn antigens. Biopsy: lymphocytes, plasma cells and macrophages in the alveolar walls, centred on bronchioles, with loose noncaseating granulomas; later scarring with cysts and new fibroblast nodules.
correlates.management: Find and remove the antigen source (stop handling the hay, rehome the birds, drain the hot tub); ongoing exposure drives permanent scarring.

correlates.name: Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy from lung adenocarcinoma
correlates.presentation: A 59-year-old woman with 25 pack-years notices over 4 months that her fingertips have become bulbous, with the angle at the nail fold lost. No fever, sputum or murmur; lungs clear, SpO2 96%. Chest CT: a 3-cm peripheral right lower lobe mass.
correlates.workup: Forearm and shin films: new bone laid down along the shafts of the radius, ulna, tibia and fibula. CT-guided biopsy of the lung mass: malignant cells forming glands. Calcium and sodium normal.

correlates.name: Hyperventilation from a panic attack
correlates.presentation: A 22-year-old student in exam week has 20 minutes of pounding heart, a feeling she cannot get enough air, lightheadedness and tingling around her mouth and in her fingertips; her hands then cramp into flexion. HR 118, RR 32, BP 128/76, SpO2 100%, lungs clear.
correlates.workup: pH 7.56, PaCO2 24, HCO3- 22; ionized calcium low (3.9 mg/dL) with a normal total calcium; K+ 3.3 mEq/L; ECG sinus tachycardia.
correlates.management: Calm reassurance and treat the underlying cause; do not infuse acid, which does not work. Watch the potassium: a low K+ can weaken the muscles, the diaphragm included.

correlates.name: Hypospadias with chordee
