correlates.presentation: On the newborn exam of a term boy, the urethral opening sits on the underside of the shaft just below the glans rather than at the tip, and the penis bends downward. Both testes are descended. His parents ask for a circumcision before discharge.
correlates.management: Do not circumcise - the urologist uses the foreskin for the repair. Refer to pediatric urology for surgical correction of the opening and the curvature; the lower the opening, the bigger the problem.

correlates.name: Idiopathic hypercalciuria
correlates.presentation: A 42-year-old man passes his third radiopaque kidney stone in 4 years. He eats fast food and salty snacks daily, drinks about 1 L of fluid a day, and cut out all dairy after his last stone. No bowel disease. BP 138/88; serum calcium 9.4 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: 24-hour urine: calcium 380 mg/day and sodium 260 mEq/day, with oxalate, urate and citrate normal; serum calcium 9.4 mg/dL and PTH normal; analysis of the passed stone: calcium oxalate.
correlates.management: Cut dietary sodium - sodium and calcium reabsorption are coupled, so salt raises urine calcium. Do NOT restrict calcium (it frees gut oxalate); go back to normal dairy. Add a thiazide.

correlates.name: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old man, former smoker, retired accountant on no regular drugs, has 14 months of slowly worsening exertional dyspnea and a dry cough; no rash, joint or muscle complaints. RR 22, SpO2 89% on room air; fine late-inspiratory crackles at both bases; clubbing.
correlates.workup: FVC 58% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.87, DLCO 38%. CT: subpleural, posterior-basal clustered cysts with reticular septal thickening and little hazy opacity. Surgical biopsy: patchy scar, dense old collagen beside pale nodules of plump fibroblasts.
correlates.management: Exclude drug, occupational and connective-tissue causes first; then refer for lung transplant evaluation, the only definitive therapy. Median survival is about 3.8 years from diagnosis.

correlates.name: IgA nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 12-year-old boy with swollen legs and dark urine starting 2 days into a cold; two similar episodes after colds last year. BP 142/90. UA many RBCs, RBC casts, some protein and WBCs. C3 normal. Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Serum IgA high, C3 normal, ASO negative. If biopsied: mesangial expansion and extra mesangial cells on PAS, granular mesangial IgA with C3 and properdin, electron-dense deposits in the mesangium
correlates.management: In a child with recurrent gross hematuria after colds, observe without a routine biopsy; follow BP, creatinine and proteinuria, since a high creatinine, BP over 140/90 and proteinuria beyond 6 months predict progression

correlates.name: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura)
correlates.presentation: A 4-year-old boy has crampy abdominal pain 2 weeks after a cold and will not use his right hand, whose wrist is swollen. A raised, lumpy, red-purple rash that does not fade under pressure covers the backs of his legs and his elbows. T 38.2 C, BP 102/64.
correlates.workup: Despite the rash, platelets are 310,000 and coagulation is normal; urinalysis shows white cells and microscopic hematuria, yet the urine culture is negative; BUN and creatinine normal.
correlates.management: Supportive care; steroids may ease the abdominal pain. Most children recover fully, but follow the kidney (urinalysis, BP) long term. Worsening abdominal pain: exclude intussusception with an enema.

correlates.name: Imperforate hymen
correlates.presentation: A 13-year-old girl had a growth spurt and Tanner 4 breast development but has never had a period. For 5 months she has had monthly lower abdominal, low back and bladder-area pain lasting several days. She voids normally. A tense, bluish bulge fills the vaginal opening.
correlates.workup: Pelvic ultrasound: the vagina is distended with layered fluid (trapped menstrual blood) that presses on the bladder; both renal pelves mildly dilated.

correlates.name: Inhalational anthrax
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old man who sorts and cleans imported raw goat wool. Two days of fever, malaise and muscle aches, then a rapid slide into breathlessness and chest pain. T 39.6 C, HR 128, BP 84/50, RR 32, SpO2 88%; dull bases; no skin lesions.
correlates.workup: Chest film: widened mediastinum with bilateral pleural effusions and little lung infiltrate. Blood culture: large gram-positive rods in chains with central spores; capsule made of poly-D-glutamate rather than sugar.
correlates.management: Ciprofloxacin immediately with ICU support; once severe breathing symptoms and shock begin, untreated mortality approaches 100%.

correlates.name: Insomnia
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old woman has 3 months of lying awake until 2 AM and waking for good at 4:30 AM, though she has 8 hours in bed. She scrolls her phone in bed and drinks coffee after dinner. By day she is tired, irritable and making errors at work. No snoring or leg discomfort.
correlates.management: Cognitive-behavioral therapy, not drugs: bed only for sleep (no phone or TV), same bed and rise times daily, no coffee or exercise near bedtime, a fixed early rise even after a bad night, relaxation and cognitive therapy.

correlates.name: Invasive aspergillosis in neutropenia
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with acute leukemia, day 14 after induction chemotherapy, absolute neutrophil count 80/uL, also on prednisone. Three days of fever despite broad antibiotics, cough, chest discomfort, blood-streaked sputum and breathlessness. T 39.2 C, HR 118, RR 28, SpO2 91%.
correlates.workup: Chest CT: several nodules. Serum galactomannan antigen positive; PCR positive. Lung biopsy: septate hyphae branching at acute (45 degree) angles, invading lung tissue and vessels.
correlates.management: Voriconazole first-line; amphotericin B, posaconazole or caspofungin as alternatives; surgery for localized disease.

correlates.name: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
correlates.presentation: 69-year-old man, 45 pack-years, 30 years in a dye plant: 2 months of painless visible hematuria with clots and 6 kg weight loss. Hb 10.9 g/dL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL. Ultrasound: right hydronephrosis behind an irregular intravesical mass at the right ureteric orifice.
correlates.workup: Transurethral resection: nests and cords of pleomorphic, high-grade epithelial cells invading the muscularis propria. Cystectomy specimen: yellowish multinodular masses filling most of the lumen, with ulceration and necrosis
correlates.management: Muscularis propria invasion calls for radical cystectomy, radiation therapy or adjuvant chemotherapy; stage (depth of wall invasion) is the main prognostic factor

correlates.name: Ischemic acute tubular injury
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man, 2 days after a massive upper GI bleed with shock (systolic BP under 80 for 3 hours before transfusion): urine output 250 mL/day despite fluids. BP now 132/78. Creatinine 1.0 rising to 4.6 mg/dL, K 5.9 mEq/L. UA shed epithelial cells and casts.
correlates.workup: Biopsy (rarely needed): patchy necrosis of short stretches of proximal straight tubule and thick ascending limb with skip areas between; detached cells and casts plug distal tubules and collecting ducts; glomeruli spared

correlates.name: Isoniazid hepatotoxicity
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old man who drinks 6 beers a day; positive IGRA before adalimumab, so he began one daily oral drug plus pyridoxine 7 weeks ago for a planned 9 months. 1 week of nausea, anorexia, dark urine and right upper quadrant ache; T 37.4 C, scleral icterus, tender liver edge
correlates.workup: ALT 840 U/L, AST 710 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 160 U/L, total bilirubin 4.6 mg/dL, INR 1.3; hepatitis A, B and C serologies negative; liver tests were normal at baseline
correlates.management: Stop the drug at once; trend liver tests and INR; no alcohol; refer for transplant evaluation if liver failure develops. Prevention: baseline and periodic liver tests, extra caution with alcohol or when given with rifampin and pyrazinamide

correlates.name: Isoniazid peripheral neuropathy
correlates.presentation: 50-year-old woman 6 weeks into four-drug therapy for cavitary pulmonary TB; no vitamin supplement was prescribed. 2 weeks of burning and numbness in both feet, worse at night. Vitals normal, lungs clear, decreased pinprick sensation over the toes; vision and color testing normal
correlates.management: Add pyridoxine (vitamin B6) 10-50 mg/day and continue TB therapy; B6 belongs on every prescription of the katG-activated drug, which blocks B6 activation and so lowers glutamate-to-GABA conversion

correlates.name: Klebsiella pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old man with diabetes who drinks a fifth of vodka daily; found passed out 4 days ago. Fever, shortness of breath and cough bringing up thick, sticky, blood-stained sputum. T 39.1 C, HR 112, RR 28, SpO2 89%; dullness and bronchial breath sounds at the right apex.
correlates.workup: Chest film: dense right upper lobe consolidation with an early cavity. Sputum Gram stain: plump gram-negative rods with thick capsules; culture: mucoid, lactose-fermenting colonies on MacConkey agar. CT may show a liver collection too.

correlates.name: Labial adhesions
correlates.presentation: A 3-year-old girl has had two afebrile bladder infections this year and burns when she pees. Exam: the labia minora are joined in the midline along their lower two-thirds by a thin, pale line, leaving a small opening above; no bulge or discharge.
correlates.management: None if mild and symptom-free - they part as estrogen rises toward adolescence. Symptomatic: estrogen cream for 2-3 weeks until they separate, then petroleum jelly so they do not re-fuse (steroid cream an alternative). Never pull apart.

correlates.name: Lactic acidosis from septic shock
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old woman has had 3 days of fever and left lower abdominal pain and is now confused. T 39.4 C, BP 78/42, HR 128, RR 30, capillary refill 4 seconds, skin mottled; left lower quadrant tender with guarding. WBC 21,000 with 18% bands.
correlates.workup: Na+ 140, Cl- 100, HCO3- 14 (anion gap 26); pH 7.28, PaCO2 30; serum lactate 6.8 mmol/L.
correlates.management: Treat the cause: early IV fluids (the right amount, not too much), prompt antibiotics, source control. Do not give bicarbonate because you dislike the pH number - alkali is almost never indicated here.

correlates.name: Latent tuberculosis infection
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old nurse born in the Philippines, about to start adalimumab for Crohn disease. Feels well: no cough, fever, night sweats or weight loss. T 36.9 C, RR 14, SpO2 99%; lungs clear; no enlarged nodes.
correlates.workup: Interferon-gamma release assay positive (skin test would read 16 mm induration at 48-72 h); chest film normal; three sputum samples, one early-morning: acid-fast smear negative, culture negative.
correlates.management: No isolation (not contagious). Treat before the TNF inhibitor to prevent disease: isoniazid + rifampin daily for 3 months (alternatives: rifampin alone for 4 months or isoniazid alone for 9 months).

correlates.name: Left lower lobe pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old woman has 4 days of fever to 38.9 C, productive cough and pain low in the left back on breathing in. RR 24, HR 110, SpO2 92%; crackles and dullness at the left base posteriorly.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: fluffy density behind the heart erasing the left hemidiaphragm and paraspinal outline; left heart border sharp; no volume loss; air-filled bronchi within it. Lateral: vertebral bodies get whiter instead of darker going down.

correlates.name: Legionella pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 64-year-old man who smokes and drinks daily, back 5 days from a hotel convention where several attendees fell ill. Three days of high fever, dry cough, watery non-bloody diarrhea and new confusion. T 39.6 C, HR 96, RR 26, SpO2 90%; scattered crackles in both lungs.
correlates.workup: Na+ 126 mEq/L. Chest film: patchy interstitial infiltrates. Sputum Gram stain: neutrophils, organisms barely stain. Urine antigen test positive. Culture needs charcoal yeast extract with iron and cysteine.
correlates.management: Macrolide (azithromycin) or a fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin); beta-lactams alone miss it. No person-to-person spread, so no isolation; the source is building water (cooling towers, air conditioning).

correlates.name: Lemierre syndrome
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old student whose sore throat began a week ago and was easing. Now high fevers, rigors and a painful swelling along the left side of the neck below the jaw. T 39.7 C, HR 124, BP 96/60, RR 22; tender, cord-like swelling along the front of the left sternocleidomastoid.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures positive (septicemia) for an anaerobic gram-negative rod. Neck ultrasound: clot in the left internal jugular vein, same side as the throat infection.

correlates.name: Lobar atelectasis
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old man 2 days after upper abdominal surgery takes shallow breaths because of incision pain and has a weak cough with thick secretions. T 37.8 C, RR 24, SpO2 91%; WBC 8,900/mm3; reduced breath sounds and dullness at the right base.
correlates.workup: Film: white right lower zone with loss of volume - the right hemidiaphragm sits higher than the left and the lung reaches less far down; no air-filled bronchi within it and no curved fluid edge up the chest wall. Bronchoscopy: a mucus plug.

correlates.name: Low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma
correlates.presentation: 61-year-old woman, former smoker: painless visible hematuria. Two similar tumors were resected from her bladder in the past 3 years; surveillance cystoscopy finds a new 1.5 cm frond-like exophytic tumor, with the rest of the mucosa normal.
correlates.workup: Resection: finger-like fronds on fibrovascular cores, lined by orderly, evenly spaced, cohesive transitional cells with scattered hyperchromatic nuclei; no invasion; FGFR3/RAS/PI3-kinase pathway

correlates.name: Lung abscess
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man with heavy drinking, badly decayed teeth and a blackout 3 weeks ago. Two weeks of fever, cough with large amounts of foul-smelling purulent sputum, chest pain and a 4-kg weight loss. T 38.4 C, HR 100, SpO2 94%; finger clubbing; crackles over the right upper back.
correlates.workup: Chest film: 5-cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right upper lobe. Sputum: mixed oral anaerobes; acid-fast smear negative. Biopsy: suppurative destruction around the cavity; a fibrotic rim means chronicity.
correlates.management: Prolonged antibiotics with anaerobic coverage (clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, or metronidazole + a beta-lactam), effective in most. In an older patient, rule out an underlying carcinoma (found in 10-15%).

correlates.name: Lung adenocarcinoma
correlates.presentation: A 56-year-old woman who has never smoked has 4 months of cough, mild left chest pain, low-grade fevers and 3-kg weight loss. SpO2 97%, lungs clear. CT: a 3.5-cm peripheral left upper lobe mass and a 4-cm left adrenal mass.
correlates.workup: Resection: glistening, mucoid cut surface; well-formed malignant glands with intracellular mucin; TTF-1 positive, chromogranin negative. Molecular testing: activating EGFR mutation.
correlates.management: Test the tumor for driver mutations; an activating EGFR mutation is treated with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, which prolongs survival. A KRAS mutation instead predicts a worse outcome.

correlates.name: Lung cancer screening candidate
correlates.presentation: A 57-year-old man comes for a wellness visit. He smoked a pack a day from age 20 to 47 (27 pack-years) and quit 10 years ago. No cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea or weight loss; exam and SpO2 normal; no prior chest imaging.
correlates.management: Low-dose chest CT (age 50-80, at least 20 pack-years, still smoking or quit within 15 years). In the national trial it cut lung cancer deaths by 20% versus chest films. His risk has about halved since quitting.

correlates.name: Lupus nephritis, class III-IV
correlates.presentation: 32-year-old woman with a red rash across her cheeks and nasal bridge, painful wrists and knees, and fatigue for 2 months; now dark urine and ankle edema. BP 152/96. UA dysmorphic RBCs and RBC casts. BUN 40 mg/dL, creatinine 2.0 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: ANA positive, then anti-dsDNA positive; C3 and C4 both low. Biopsy: thick, rigid capillary walls, mesangial and endocapillary hypercellularity, crescents; granular IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q; subendothelial deposits

correlates.name: Lupus nephritis, class V
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old woman followed 3 years for joint pain, a facial rash and anti-dsDNA antibodies develops leg swelling and frothy urine over 6 weeks. BP 134/86. UA 4+ protein, no RBC casts. 24-h protein 6 g, albumin 2.1 g/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: C3 and C4 low. Biopsy: uniform GBM thickening with no extra glomerular cells; granular IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q along the capillary walls; subepithelial electron-dense deposits

correlates.name: Malakoplakia
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old kidney transplant recipient on immunosuppression: a year of recurrent E. coli urinary infections despite treatment, with frequency and suprapubic discomfort. Afebrile. Cystoscopy: soft, yellow, slightly raised mucosal plaques 3-4 cm across.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: sheets of large foamy macrophages with granular cytoplasm, plus lymphocytes; inside the macrophages, round laminated calcified concretions formed in enlarged lysosomes

correlates.name: Malignant hypertension (malignant nephrosclerosis)
correlates.presentation: 50-year-old Black man with untreated high BP: 2 days of severe headache, nausea, vomiting and blurred vision, now confused. BP 236/128. Both optic discs swollen with blurred margins. Creatinine 3.4 mg/dL (1.1 last year). UA blood and 2+ protein.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: arterioles with concentric, laminated wall thickening from proliferating smooth muscle-like cells and reduplicated basement membrane, lumens nearly shut; small arteries with fibrinoid necrosis
correlates.management: Treat as an emergency, but bring BP down in a controlled way over a few hours, not immediately to normal: an abrupt fall underperfuses the brain and other organs

correlates.name: Malignant mesothelioma
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old who worked 30 years in a brake-lining and insulation plant (left 35 years ago) has 8 months of dull right chest discomfort, malaise, low-grade fevers, night sweats and 7-kg weight loss. Dull to percussion and absent breath sounds over the right lower chest.
correlates.workup: CT: right effusion with a thick, nodular pleural rind encasing the whole lung and running into the fissures. Biopsy: epithelial-like cells forming tubules and papillae; calretinin+, keratin+, TTF-1 negative; 9p deletion (CDKN2A loss).
correlates.management: Prognosis is poor: about half die within 12 months of diagnosis. The same exposure carries a still higher risk of lung carcinoma than of this pleural cancer.

correlates.name: MDR/XDR tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man released from prison 4 months ago, treated for the same lung infection 2 years earlier but stopped the pills after 6 weeks once he felt better. Two months of cough, blood-streaked sputum, night sweats, 6-kg weight loss. T 38.3 C; wasted; left apical crackles.
correlates.workup: Chest film: left apical cavity. Sputum: acid-fast rods. Culture with susceptibility testing: the isolate grows despite isoniazid and rifampin (the worst strains also despite fluoroquinolones and amikacin or kanamycin).
correlates.management: Airborne isolation; all-oral bedaquiline + pretomanid + linezolid for 6 months (moxifloxacin added if needed) or a longer tailored course; ECGs for QT, liver tests, blood counts; directly observed therapy, no missed doses.

correlates.name: Measles
correlates.presentation: Unvaccinated 4-year-old, 10 days after a crowded indoor party: 3 days of fever to 40.5 C, cough, runny nose, sore throat, red watery eyes and light sensitivity, then a dense red rash that starts on the face and spreads to the trunk, arms and legs.
correlates.management: Supportive: acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever, possibly vitamin A; nothing lowers the viral load. Airborne isolation (negative pressure, N95); the virus also survives on surfaces up to 2 hours. Reportable.

correlates.name: Medullary sponge kidney
correlates.presentation: A 35-year-old woman, seen between episodes, has had four bouts of stone-related flank pain with blood in her urine since her twenties; every stone has been radiopaque. She drinks 2.5 L a day, salts lightly, eats dairy. BP 118/72; serum calcium, HCO3-, PTH and creatinine normal.
correlates.workup: CT urogram: many tiny cysts within the renal pyramids of both kidneys, clustered with small radiopaque stones; cortex and kidney size normal.

correlates.name: Membranoproliferative GN type I
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old man with untreated hepatitis C: weight gain, ascites, right upper quadrant pain, leg swelling and dark, frothy urine. BP 164/100. UA blood with RBC casts, 3.7 g/day protein. Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Cryoglobulins in serum. Biopsy: thick capillary walls with extra mesangial and endocapillary cells, GBM doubled on silver stain; granular C3, IgG, C1q and C4; subendothelial and mesangial deposits

correlates.name: Membranous nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B: 6 weeks of weight gain, frothy urine, pitting edema and ascites with a right upper quadrant ache. BP 146/90. UA 4+ protein, no RBC casts. 24-h protein 8 g, albumin 1.9 g/dL. Now sudden left flank pain and hematuria.
correlates.workup: Doppler: left renal vein clot. Biopsy: uniformly thick capillary walls, no extra cells; granular IgG and C3 along the loops; subepithelial deposits with GBM projections between them. Primary cases: IgG to the PLA2 receptor
correlates.management: Look for and treat a secondary cause first: stop NSAIDs or captopril, treat hepatitis B or C, screen for lung or colon cancer and melanoma, test for lupus. Steroids do not change survival

correlates.name: Metabolic alkalosis from antacid overuse
correlates.presentation: A 60-year-old man with GERD and peptic ulcer disease skips his omeprazole and instead chews calcium carbonate tablets with glasses of milk all day, his son says. He is weak and confused. RR 10, BP 132/84. HCO3- 36 mEq/L, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, the same as last year.
correlates.workup: pH 7.51, PaCO2 49, HCO3- 37: pH above 7.4 with both bicarbonate and PaCO2 high.
correlates.management: Treat the cause: stop the chewable calcium carbonate, baking soda, diuretic, laxative or steroid that is loading bicarbonate; acetazolamide only if very severe.

correlates.name: Metastatic tumor to the lung
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old woman who had a sigmoid colon resection for cancer 2 years ago has 2 months of exertional dyspnea, dry cough and 5-kg weight loss. SpO2 93%. Chest film: many round, well-defined nodules of varying sizes scattered through both lungs.
correlates.workup: CT-guided biopsy of one nodule: tan-white tissue of malignant glands matching the earlier bowel primary; TTF-1 negative.

correlates.name: Methanol poisoning
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old man drank liquor from a friend's homemade still 18 hours ago. Now he has headache, vomiting and vision that has gone blurred and dim, worsening by the hour. RR 28, BP 134/82, pupils sluggish. Na+ 139, Cl- 100, HCO3- 9; pH 7.15, PaCO2 23.
correlates.management: Fomepizole to block alcohol dehydrogenase so the liver meets only a trickle of toxic metabolite; if none, IV ethanol (or oral vodka) to compete for the enzyme; saline diuresis; dialysis for severe cases.

correlates.name: Mild obstructive sleep apnea in a slim adult with a small jaw
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old woman, BMI 21, with a narrow lower jaw and a chin set well back, has a year of unrefreshing nights, daytime drowsiness and poor concentration. Her partner hears snoring and occasional pauses. BP 118/74; tonsils small, uvula normal.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: 11 events per hour, each an 11-15 s stop in nose and mouth airflow during continued chest and belly effort, ending in a brief arousal; SpO2 nadir 93%.
correlates.management: A dentist-made mandibular advancement device that pulls the jaw forward to hold the airway open; it works well in mild, symptomatic disease with a small jaw, poorly in severe disease or marked obesity.

correlates.name: Miliary tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: 47-year-old woman from Mexico on infliximab for rheumatoid arthritis, never screened before starting it. Three weeks of fevers, night sweats, 5-kg weight loss and rising breathlessness. T 39.1 C, HR 112, RR 26, SpO2 90% on room air; lungs sound almost clear.
correlates.workup: Chest film: innumerable 1-2 mm nodules spread evenly through both lungs from apex to base. Acid-fast rods in bronchoscopic washings; culture positive weeks later (blood-borne spread to lung and other organs).

correlates.name: Minimal change disease
correlates.presentation: 6-year-old boy, 10 days after a cold: puffy eyes on waking that fade by evening, now swollen legs and belly and frothy urine. BP 96/60. Dipstick 4+ protein, no blood. Albumin 1.6 g/dL, cholesterol 380 mg/dL, creatinine 0.4 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Urine protein is almost all albumin (selective). If biopsied: normal glomeruli on light microscopy, negative immunofluorescence, and foot processes fused into one sheet on EM with no deposits
correlates.management: Oral corticosteroids without a biopsy, then a taper; biopsy only for frequent relapses, steroid resistance or hypertension. New fever with belly pain: sepsis workup and IV antibiotics for pneumococcal peritonitis

correlates.name: Misplaced nasogastric tube
correlates.presentation: A 78-year-old man with a recent stroke and poor swallow coughed repeatedly while a feeding catheter was passed through his nose. Feeds were started; 6 hours later he has T 38.3 C, RR 28, SpO2 88% and new crackles at the left base.
correlates.workup: Film: radiopaque tip loops into the right and then the left main bronchus instead of passing below the left hemidiaphragm into the gastric bubble; after feeds, a new white density behind the heart has erased the left hemidiaphragm outline.
correlates.management: Stop feeds and do not use it; pull back and reposition until the tip lies below the left hemidiaphragm in the stomach or proximal duodenum, and confirm on a new film before feeding.

correlates.name: Mixed urinary incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old woman, two vaginal deliveries, postmenopausal, has leaked when she coughs or sneezes for 8 years. For the past year she also gets sudden, desperate needs to void and leaks on the way to the bathroom. Urinalysis normal.
correlates.workup: Office cough test with a full bladder: leakage with each cough. Filling cystometry: involuntary detrusor contractions during filling. Postvoid residual 35 mL.
correlates.management: Work out which component is primary and treat it first, then the other: pelvic floor therapy, lifestyle change and Kegels, plus an anticholinergic for the bladder spasms; surgery if those fail.

correlates.name: MRSA infection
correlates.presentation: 17-year-old high-school wrestler who shares mats and towels; two teammates had boils this month. Four days of a painful, enlarging hot swelling on the thigh. T 38.4 C, HR 98; 4-cm fluctuant, tender, red mass draining pus, with surrounding redness; tender inguinal nodes.
correlates.workup: Pus Gram stain: gram-positive cocci in clusters; beta-hemolytic, catalase- and coagulase-positive. Cefoxitin disk screen resistant, growth on oxacillin-salt agar, PCR detects the altered penicillin-binding protein gene.
correlates.management: If admitted: contact precautions (single room or cohort, gloves, gown, dedicated equipment). Serious invasive infection: vancomycin or linezolid; no penicillin, cephalosporin or carbapenem works. Practise stewardship.

correlates.name: Mumps
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old unvaccinated college student during a dormitory outbreak. Two days of fever, headache, muscle aches, poor appetite and fatigue, then painful swelling in front of and below both ears; today a sore, swollen right testis. T 38.4 C, HR 96.
correlates.workup: Mostly clinical. Serum IgM positive (new infection; IgG alone would mean past immunity); RT-PCR, viral culture or a 4-fold rise in IgG can confirm.
correlates.management: Supportive. Keep away from others from 1-2 days before the swelling until 5 days after it (spread by droplets and fomites); reportable to the CDC; watch for testicular atrophy and late meningitis.

correlates.name: Mycoplasma pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old army recruit; several in his barracks are coughing. Ten days of gradually worsening headache, malaise, low-grade fever without chills and a dry, persistent cough; still training. T 38.0 C, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 97%; fine crackles scattered over both lungs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: patchy bilateral interstitial infiltrates. Gram stain: no organisms. Cold agglutinin titer raised; LDH up and haptoglobin low (IgM-driven hemolysis). Pleural effusion in 10-20%.
correlates.management: Macrolide (azithromycin), doxycycline or a fluoroquinolone; beta-lactams fail because the organism has no cell wall. Macrolides are the choice in pregnancy and children. Usually self-limited.

correlates.name: Narcolepsy
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old college student, BMI 22, has fallen asleep in lectures and at meals since about age 15 despite 8 hours in bed; his roommate hears no snoring. Twice, laughing hard at a joke, his knees gave way and he sank to the floor, awake throughout. Exam normal.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: 1 breathing event/h and no other cause of sleepiness. Next day, five scheduled naps (9, 11, 1, 3, 5): asleep within 1 min each time, and in REM within 3 min in three of the naps.
correlates.management: Fixed bedtime (10:30 PM to 7 AM), no schedule shifts, heavy meals or alcohol, planned 15-min naps; modafinil or methylphenidate for daytime sleepiness; sodium oxybate (GHB) only by specially trained prescribers.

correlates.name: Neuraminidase-inhibitor neuropsychiatric events
correlates.presentation: 11-year-old boy with rapid-antigen-positive influenza started a twice-daily oral antiviral suspension yesterday. Tonight he is confused and frightened, sees insects on the wall and tried to run outside. T 38.4 C, HR 110, neck supple, no focal deficits; it clears within hours
correlates.management: Stop the drug and observe him in a safe setting; these reactions are rare, transient and of unestablished cause, mostly in children and adolescents, and came to light in post-marketing surveillance

correlates.name: Neuroblastoma
correlates.presentation: 2-year-old boy with 3 weeks of fever, weight loss, irritability and malaise. Thin and pale. A firm, irregular abdominal mass extends from the right upper quadrant across the midline. BP 106/64.
correlates.workup: Imaging: mass arising from the adrenal gland, pushing the kidney aside rather than growing from it, and crossing the midline

correlates.name: Nocturnal incontinence in an older adult (fluid shifts)
correlates.presentation: A 79-year-old woman with heart failure and swollen ankles takes her furosemide at bedtime and drinks two cups of tea after dinner. She wakes 3-4 times a night to void and has started wetting the bed. Dry and in control by day. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin.
correlates.workup: Voiding diary: most of the 24-hour urine volume is passed between bedtime and morning; urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 40 mL; Na+ 138.
correlates.management: Last drink well before bed, no caffeine; move the diuretic to the morning; elevate the legs in the late afternoon and use support hose; review medications. Desmopressin only with caution: hyponatremia in the elderly can mean admission.

correlates.name: Non-resolving pneumonia from an endobronchial carcinoma
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old man with 45 pack-years has his third right lower lobe pneumonia in 5 months; each antibiotic course settled the fever, but cough and streaks of blood in the sputum persist. T 37.9 C, SpO2 93%; dull with reduced breath sounds at the right base. Down 4 kg.
correlates.workup: Film 8 weeks after treatment: the same right lower zone opacity, now with volume loss. CT: a mass narrowing the right lower lobe bronchus with collapse and consolidation beyond it. Bronchoscopy: friable tumor filling the bronchus.
correlates.management: Bronchoscopy with washings, brushings and biopsy of the central lesion, then staging CT of chest, liver and adrenals. In a smoker over 40, repeated pneumonias or colds that fail to clear should raise this early.

correlates.name: Non-small cell lung cancer, stage I-IIIA (resectable)
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old woman with 35 pack-years had a CT-guided biopsy of a 2.8-cm peripheral left upper lobe mass: malignant cells with ample cytoplasm and no nuclear molding. She walks 2 miles a day; no headache, bone pain or weight loss. Calcium, ALP, AST, ALT and bilirubin normal.
correlates.workup: Chest CT through the liver and adrenals and whole-body PET-CT: uptake only in the mass, no hilar or mediastinal nodes, no distant deposits; brain MRI clear. FEV1 2.1 L, DLCO 72% predicted.
correlates.management: Curative intent: lobectomy (open or VATS), the standard when FEV1 is above 1.5 L and DLCO above 60%, with or without adjuvant chemotherapy. Wedge resection if lobectomy is not tolerated; chemoradiation if surgery is impossible.

correlates.name: Non-small cell lung cancer, stage IV
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old man with 45 pack-years has 2 months of cough and 6-kg weight loss, then 2 weeks of morning headaches and a seizure. Afebrile; mild right hand weakness. Brain MRI: several enhancing round lesions at the gray-white junction. CT: 4-cm left upper lobe mass.
correlates.workup: Bronchoscopic biopsy of the mass: malignant cells with ample cytoplasm, no nuclear molding; tissue sent for tumor marker testing. Staging CT: a 3-cm right adrenal mass; skeletal scintigraphy: uptake in two ribs; alkaline phosphatase raised.
correlates.management: Distant spread means palliative, symptom-oriented intent, not surgery. Targeted therapy if tumor markers are positive (EGFR or ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor); bring in palliative care early, which lengthened survival in a trial.

correlates.name: Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old woman who has never smoked has 7 months of exertional dyspnea and dry cough. She reports fingers that turn white then blue in the cold and morning hand stiffness. Fine crackles at both bases, no clubbing; SpO2 93% on room air.
correlates.workup: FVC 68% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.85, DLCO 55%. CT: symmetric bilateral lower-lobe fine reticulation with patchy hazy opacities and no cysts. Biopsy: lymphocytes and plasma cells or scarring all at one stage of age; no fibroblast nodules.

correlates.name: Normal sleep changes of aging
correlates.presentation: A healthy 76-year-old woman says her nights are lighter than at 40: she wakes briefly many times, then drifts off again, and it takes longer to fall asleep. She feels rested and active by day, with no naps, snoring, leg discomfort or low mood.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: asleep for 79% of the time in bed; more N1 and less slow-wave (delta) activity than a young adult; REM about 20%; about 15 brief arousals per hour; 3 breathing events/h.
correlates.management: Reassurance: these findings are expected at her age and need no treatment.

correlates.name: NSAID papillary necrosis
correlates.presentation: 63-year-old woman with knee osteoarthritis has taken high-dose ibuprofen plus naproxen for months; a week of vomiting and poor intake, now visible blood in her urine. Afebrile, no rash, BP 104/66. Eosinophils normal. Creatinine 1.0 rising to 2.7 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: UA blood, no WBC casts or eosinophils. Pathology: dark, infarcted zones at the tips of the renal papillae with hyperemic borders, from lost vasodilatory prostaglandins and medullary ischemia
correlates.management: Stop every cyclooxygenase inhibitor, including selective COX-2 drugs, which still harm the COX-2-rich kidney

correlates.name: NSAID-induced TIN with minimal change disease
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man taking naproxen daily for 8 months for back pain: 3 weeks of leg swelling, frothy urine and falling urine output. Afebrile, no rash. BP 132/84. Creatinine 3.2 mg/dL (0.9 last year). UA 4+ protein, WBCs, no RBC casts. 24-h protein 9 g.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: interstitial edema with lymphocytes and eosinophils and tubulitis; glomeruli normal on light microscopy, IF negative, and EM shows diffuse foot process effacement without deposits

correlates.name: Obstructive pyelonephritis (infected, blocked kidney)
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old woman sent home 4 days ago to pass a 7 mm right ureteral stone returns with T 39.3 C, rigors, worsening right flank pain and vomiting. HR 122, BP 92/56; the right costovertebral angle is exquisitely tender.
correlates.workup: Urinalysis: pyuria, positive nitrite, hematuria; WBC 19,000; creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (0.9 last week). CT: the same stone still lodged in the right ureter, with the ureter and collecting system dilated above it.
correlates.management: An emergency: antibiotics at once and emergent urology to drain the kidney - ureteroscopy with a ureteral stent or a percutaneous route - because obstruction plus infection quickly turns septic. Definitive stone removal comes later.

correlates.name: Obstructive sleep apnea in a child
correlates.presentation: A 6-year-old boy's teacher reports poor focus and disruptive behavior in class this year. His parents hear loud snoring every night with pauses in his breathing. Weight 50th percentile. The tonsils are very large and nearly touch in the midline.
correlates.management: Refer to ENT to remove the enlarged tonsils: in children the cause is usually the tonsils, not weight.

correlates.name: Occupational asthma
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old man who started spray-painting cars in an auto-body shop 8 months ago has new wheeze, chest tightness and cough that build through each shift and cleared during a 2-week vacation; no childhood wheeze or allergies. No fever, no crackles; SpO2 98%.
correlates.workup: Total IgE normal and skin tests negative to aeroallergens; resting spirometry normal. Methacholine challenge positive (FEV1 falls 24%), and FEV1 falls after supervised exposure to the specific spray agent.

correlates.name: Oncocytoma
correlates.presentation: 63-year-old man: a CT done for gallstones finds an asymptomatic, well-circumscribed, homogeneous 5 cm left renal mass with a central scar. No hematuria, flank pain or weight loss. Hb 14.2 g/dL, calcium normal, BP 128/80.
correlates.workup: Resection: encapsulated, homogeneous mahogany-brown mass with a central scar; uniform round cells with granular, intensely pink cytoplasm; EM shows cells packed with mitochondria

correlates.name: Orthostatic proteinuria
correlates.presentation: A 14-year-old boy has a sports physical late in the afternoon; the office dipstick shows 1+ protein with no blood. He has no swelling, fever, dark urine or joint pain. BP 112/70, no edema, exam normal; BMP normal.
correlates.workup: Urine caught in a cup the moment he wakes, before standing: dipstick negative for protein; spot protein/creatinine ratio below 0.2.
correlates.management: Repeat with a first-morning void before any further workup and reassure if clear. If the morning sample still shows protein: spot protein/creatinine ratio, then a 24-hour urine protein. Protein plus blood together deserves a closer look.

correlates.name: Ovarian torsion
correlates.presentation: A 15-year-old girl has 3 hours of sudden, severe right lower abdominal pain with repeated vomiting; her family thinks it is a stomach bug. Afebrile, HR 112, BP 118/74. Right lower quadrant tender without rebound; urine pregnancy test negative; periods regular.
correlates.workup: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler: an enlarged right ovary with little or no blood flow; appendix not seen to be inflamed.

correlates.name: Overflow incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 68-year-old woman with 20 years of type 2 diabetes and numb feet dribbles urine day and night. She always feels her bladder is full, never feels empty after voiding and has a weak stream. A distended bladder is palpable above the pubis. HbA1c 9.4%.
correlates.workup: Postvoid residual 480 mL by ultrasound; urinalysis normal; urodynamics: a weak, poorly sustained detrusor contraction with no outlet obstruction.
correlates.management: A catheterization regimen (scheduled intermittent catheterization) to empty and retrain the bladder, diversion if needed; stop drugs that impair emptying - anticholinergics, alpha agonists, calcium channel blockers.

correlates.name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
correlates.presentation: 59-year-old man on hemodialysis for 11 years: routine ultrasound shows many cysts in both shrunken kidneys and a new 4 cm hemorrhagic, cystic mass in the right kidney. Intermittent microscopic hematuria. BP 138/84.
correlates.workup: Histology: tumor cells covering papillae whose cores are stuffed with foamy macrophages, with scattered psammoma bodies; trisomy 7

correlates.name: Paracoccidioidomycosis
correlates.presentation: 62-year-old man who has farmed in rural Brazil all his life. A year of cough and breathlessness, then painful ulcers on the gums, lips and inside the nose that keep spreading; 8-kg weight loss. T 37.8 C, RR 22, SpO2 93%; granular ulcers on the lips and palate.
correlates.workup: Scraping of the lip ulcer: a large central yeast surrounded by many small narrow-based daughter buds. Chest film: chronic bilateral infiltrates.
correlates.management: Itraconazole; a sulfonamide also works but needs prolonged therapy to prevent relapse; amphotericin B for disseminated disease.

correlates.name: Paraphimosis
correlates.presentation: A 10-month-old uncircumcised boy in the ED for a fever workup had a catheterized urine sample taken 4 hours ago and has cried inconsolably since. The glans is swollen, dark purple and tense, with a tight ring of retracted foreskin behind it.
correlates.management: Emergency: reduce it by hand at once - steady pressure with gauze for grip, pushing the glans back through the ring and the foreskin forward; urology if it fails. Always return a retracted foreskin after a catheterization.

correlates.name: Patent urachus
correlates.presentation: 10-day-old boy: the umbilicus stays wet and keeps leaking clear fluid, more when he cries or strains, and he fusses as if in abdominal pain. Afebrile; voids normally; the rest of the exam is normal.
correlates.workup: Imaging: an open channel running from the dome of the bladder up to the umbilicus, along the midline of the anterior abdominal wall

correlates.name: Pericardial effusion
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer has 6 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. HR 104, BP 118/76, RR 20; JVP 9 cm, soft distant heart sounds; lungs clear, no crackles; no leg edema.
correlates.workup: PA film: cardiac outline enlarged (cardiothoracic ratio 0.68) and smoothly widened at its base, tapering abruptly to a narrow waist at the level of the aorta where the sac inserts on the great vessels; lungs clear.

correlates.name: Pertussis
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old fully vaccinated as an infant. Two weeks of runny nose and low fever, then 3 weeks of violent coughing fits that leave her red-faced and breathless, sometimes ending in vomiting; well between fits. T 37.2 C, RR 18, SpO2 98%; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: WBC 26,000/uL with 78% lymphocytes; chest film clear; nasopharyngeal swab PCR positive (the organism grows only on a special selective medium).
correlates.management: Macrolide (azithromycin) to kill the organism and limit spread, but the toxins drive the illness, so the cough runs its course; supportive care, especially in infants. Prevention: DTaP for children, Tdap boosters.

correlates.name: Pharyngoconjunctival fever
correlates.presentation: 9-year-old back from a week at summer camp where many campers shared one swimming pool and several fell ill. Two days of T 39.3 C, sore throat, malaise and red, watery eyes. Red pharynx, tender cervical nodes, both conjunctivae red; no cough.

correlates.name: Physiologic phimosis
correlates.presentation: Parents of a healthy uncircumcised 3-year-old worry because his foreskin will not pull back over the glans. He voids with a strong, straight stream and has no pain, redness, swelling or infections. Exam: narrow, nontender foreskin opening; glans not visible.
correlates.management: Reassure: normal in uncircumcised boys; the adhesions loosen with time, especially toward the teens. Clean the outside only and leave it alone - forcing it back can tear and scar it or trap it behind the glans.

correlates.name: Pleural effusion
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old woman with heart failure has 2 weeks of increasing exertional dyspnea; RR 22, SpO2 93%. Right lower chest: flat percussion note, reduced fremitus, no breath sounds. Upright film: right costophrenic angle blunted, a curved upper edge climbing the lateral chest wall.
correlates.workup: Film taken lying flat in the ICU: no curved upper edge; instead a hazy, veil-like density over the lower right hemithorax with vessels visible through it, as the fluid layers behind the lung; costophrenic angle blunted.

correlates.name: Pneumococcal pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 36-year-old man whose spleen was removed after a car crash. Sudden onset this morning of shaking chills, fever, cough with thick purulent sputum and right chest pain on breathing in. T 39.8 C, HR 116, RR 26, SpO2 91%; dullness, loud breath sounds and a rub at the right base.
correlates.workup: Chest film: dense consolidation filling one whole lobe. Sputum Gram stain: gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci in pairs; urine antigen test positive; blood cultures grow alpha-hemolytic, optochin-sensitive colonies.
correlates.management: Admit, draw blood cultures, start a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, then narrow to targeted therapy - most are afebrile within 2-3 days. Vaccinate against the encapsulated organism (no spleen).

correlates.name: Pneumocystis pneumonia in HIV
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old man with HIV who stopped his medicines 2 years ago. Three weeks of slowly increasing breathlessness on exertion, dry cough and low fevers. T 38.1 C, HR 104, RR 28, SpO2 92% at rest falling to 84% after a short walk; lungs nearly clear.
correlates.workup: CD4 140/uL. Chest film: diffuse bilateral hazy interstitial opacities. Induced sputum or BAL: small round cysts on silver or fluorescent-antibody stain; the organism cannot be cultured. Biopsy: foamy alveolar exudate, plasma cells.
correlates.management: TMP-SMX (pentamidine if intolerant); restore immunity with antiretroviral therapy; prophylaxis with TMP-SMX (dapsone as an alternative) whenever CD4 is under 200.

correlates.name: Pneumomediastinum
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old, 2 days after a ruptured right pneumothorax was drained, develops central chest pain that runs up into his neck and worsens with deep breaths; no swelling of the face or chest wall. HR 98, BP 126/80, SpO2 96%, both lungs expanded on exam.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: thin lucent stripe outlining the heart with a fine white line lifted off it, running up into the neck as parallel gas streaks; gas crosses beneath the heart from one hemidiaphragm to the other. CT: mediastinum lifted by gas.

correlates.name: Pneumonic plague
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old field biologist in rural New Mexico who traps prairie dogs; 3 days ago she nursed a coworker who had a swollen, tender groin node and later a cough. Sudden high fever, chills, weakness, bloody cough and breathlessness. T 40.1 C, HR 132, BP 82/48, RR 34, SpO2 85%.
correlates.workup: Sputum and blood: gram-negative bacilli whose stain gathers at both ends of each cell; culture grows the same rods. WBC 24,000/uL.
correlates.management: Streptomycin at once: the inhaled form nears 100% mortality untreated. Prevention is rodent and flea control.

correlates.name: Pneumonic tularemia
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old hunter who skinned and cleaned several wild rabbits 4 days ago. High fever, chills, headache, malaise, dry cough and chest pain on breathing in. T 39.5 C, HR 104, RR 24, SpO2 92%; crackles over both lower lobes; no skin ulcer.
correlates.workup: Gram stain: tiny gram-negative coccobacilli, mostly inside macrophages. Agglutination test (antibody titer) positive; the lab avoids culturing it. Chest film: patchy bilateral infiltrates.
correlates.management: Streptomycin. Humans are dead-end hosts: ticks keep the organism in wild rabbits, so prevention is avoiding ticks and handling game with care.

correlates.name: Pneumopericardium
correlates.presentation: A 60-year-old woman had a needle drain of a large fluid collection around her heart an hour ago. She feels well; BP 122/76, HR 88, SpO2 97%, no neck swelling or crackling skin.
correlates.workup: Post-procedure film: a thin dark band of gas closely outlining the heart, held in by a fine white line of the sac that stops at the origin of the great vessels; no gas tracks into the neck or soft tissues.

correlates.name: Pneumoperitoneum
correlates.presentation: A 62-year-old man had sudden severe upper abdominal pain 6 hours ago that has spread across the whole abdomen. He lies still; the abdomen is rigid with rebound tenderness and absent bowel sounds. T 38.1 C, HR 118, BP 102/64.
correlates.workup: Upright chest film: a thin curved crescent of gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm, separating it from the top of the liver; on the lateral view the gas sits anteriorly under the diaphragm.

correlates.name: Posterior urethral valves
correlates.presentation: A 3-month-old boy is admitted with his second febrile kidney infection. His mother says he never makes a spray when he pees - urine just dribbles out. Exam: a smooth, round midline mass above the pubis; normal genitalia, both testes descended.
correlates.workup: Renal ultrasound: both kidneys and both ureters dilated above a distended, thick-walled bladder. Voiding study: the urethra just below the bladder neck is dilated and then abruptly narrows during voiding.

correlates.name: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
correlates.presentation: 10-year-old with dark red urine and less of it; untreated sore throat with fever 2 weeks ago. Puffy eyes. Temp 101 F, BP 140/90. UA RBC casts, WBCs, protein. BUN 38 mg/dL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: C3 low with normal C4; ASO and anti-DNase B high (anti-hyaluronidase after a skin infection); positive throat culture or rapid antigen test. Biopsy not needed; if done, large subepithelial deposits beneath the foot processes
correlates.management: Supportive: fluid restriction, diuretics and antihypertensives with strict intake and output. Antibiotics do not prevent the kidney disease. Recheck C3 at 6-8 weeks; if it is still low, look for another diagnosis

correlates.name: Potter sequence
correlates.presentation: A boy born at 35 weeks after a pregnancy with almost no amniotic fluid has a flattened nose, clubbed feet and stiff, contracted limbs. He is in severe distress from the first breath despite ventilation: SpO2 70%, small chest.
correlates.workup: Prenatal ultrasound: severe oligohydramnios; no fetal kidneys or bladder seen. Chest film after birth: small, poorly aerated lungs.

correlates.name: Primary influenza viral pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 72-year-old unvaccinated woman with heart failure, in February. Three days ago: abrupt fever, muscle aches and dry cough; since then steadily worse breathlessness, scant sputum, never improving. T 39.0 C, HR 118, RR 32, SpO2 86% on room air; diffuse crackles in both lungs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: diffuse bilateral patchy and interstitial opacities, no lobar consolidation; sputum Gram stain shows no dominant organism. Autopsy: heavy, red, firm lungs; alveolar walls widened by lymphocytes and monocytes; hyaline membranes.

correlates.name: Primary nocturnal enuresis
correlates.presentation: An 8-year-old boy has never had a dry night, though he has been dry by day since age 3; he is embarrassed to go to sleepovers. His father wet the bed until about age 10. He is a deep sleeper. Growth, BP, exam and a urinalysis are normal.
correlates.management: No drinks 2-3 hours before bed, no caffeine; a bed-wetting alarm (the one thing that cures it), a reward calendar and no-blame help with cleanup. Desmopressin for sleepovers lowers urine output but does not cure; tricyclics rarely.

correlates.name: Primary pulmonary coccidioidomycosis
correlates.presentation: 35-year-old man from Ohio who drove through a dust storm outside Phoenix 2 weeks ago, after a wet winter there. Fever, dry cough, chest pain on breathing in, fatigue, aching joints, and tender red nodules on both shins. T 38.2 C, HR 96, SpO2 96%; scattered crackles on the right.
correlates.workup: Sputum or biopsy: large round thick-walled structures packed with endospores. ELISA IgM/IgG positive; complement fixation IgG titer measured. The lab is told not to culture it (airborne arthroconidia infect staff).
correlates.management: Most need no treatment. Fluconazole or itraconazole for persistent lung infection or a symptomatic mild case. The shin nodules are an immune reaction, not spread of the infection.

correlates.name: Primary pulmonary tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: 4-year-old whose grandfather moved in from Pakistan 3 months ago and has had a 2-month cough with blood-streaked sputum. Two weeks of low-grade fever and mild cough. T 38.0 C, RR 28; a few crackles at the right base; otherwise well.
correlates.workup: Chest film: enlarged right hilar node with patchy infiltrate in the right lower zone, no cavity. Skin test 12 mm. Gastric aspirate: acid-fast rods. Once healed: calcified subpleural lower-lobe nodule plus calcified hilar node.

correlates.name: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax
correlates.presentation: A 22-year-old man with no lung disease felt sudden sharp left chest pain and breathlessness while sitting at his desk. HR 96, BP 124/78, RR 20, SpO2 95%. Left breath sounds reduced, left chest hyperresonant, trachea midline.
correlates.workup: Upright frontal film: thin white line paralleling the left chest wall with no lung markings beyond it and darker spaces between the left ribs; heart and trachea in normal position. CT: a small ruptured bleb at the left apex.

correlates.name: Progressive massive fibrosis
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old who mined coal underground in Kentucky for 38 years has 3 years of worsening exertional dyspnea and productive cough; he now stops after 50 feet. SpO2 88%. FEV1 45% predicted, FVC 56%, TLC 115%, RV 150%.
correlates.workup: Film: dense upper-zone masses of 3-8 cm on a background of small rounded opacities. Resection: black scars far larger than 1 cm made of dense collagen, reticulin and pigment, some with necrotic centres from ischemia.

correlates.name: Pseudomonas nosocomial infection
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old man with burns over 40% of his body, hospital day 12, in a burn unit with a recent cluster of infections. New fever and a burn site oozing green-blue exudate. T 39.1 C, HR 122, BP 92/56; WBC 18,500/uL.
correlates.workup: Culture: motile, oxidase-positive gram-negative rods that do not ferment lactose and make a blue-green pigment; resistant to many common antibiotics. In a lung: red patches with tan rims, cavities, neutrophils around vessels.
correlates.management: Piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime or imipenem; two agents active against it when there is structural lung disease or known resistance. It turns resistant during about 10% of courses.

correlates.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
correlates.presentation: A 41-year-old man who has never smoked has 9 months of slowly progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough, no fever, weight loss or occupational exposure. SpO2 90%, few crackles. FEV1/FVC 0.84, DLCO 44%. Serum IgG that neutralizes GM-CSF is detected.
correlates.workup: Lung biopsy: alveoli filled with pink, homogeneous, PAS-positive precipitate while the septa stay thin; EM shows the material is packed with lamellar bodies (surfactant particles).
correlates.management: Whole-lung lavage to wash out the material; add GM-CSF therapy; with neutralizing antibodies consider plasmapheresis or immunosuppression; treat any secondary cause.

correlates.name: Pulmonary artery catheter tip too far
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old in the ICU after cardiac surgery has a right internal jugular line placed to measure pulmonary artery pressures. A day later he has new right pleuritic chest pain and a little blood-streaked sputum; SpO2 drops from 96% to 91%.
correlates.workup: Film: the line's tip lies far out in a small right lower lobe artery instead of over the central mediastinum in the main pulmonary artery, with a new wedge-shaped peripheral opacity downstream from it.
correlates.management: Pull the line back so its tip lies in the right or left main pulmonary artery; a tip left in the right atrium is not far enough.

correlates.name: Pulmonary hamartoma
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old man with no symptoms has a 1.8-cm smooth, sharply outlined round peripheral nodule on a chest film taken for a work physical. Never smoked; exam normal; no weight loss.
correlates.workup: Resection: disorganized lobules of mature hyaline cartilage mixed with fat and fibrous tissue, with slit-like clefts lined by entrapped bronchial epithelium; no atypia.
correlates.management: Benign; once the diagnosis is established it needs no further treatment.

correlates.name: Pulmonary hypertension found on PFTs
correlates.presentation: A 44-year-old woman who never smoked has 10 months of progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue, without cough, wheeze or sputum. Lungs clear. FEV1/FVC 0.80, FEV1 93% and FVC 95% predicted, TLC 97%, but DLCO 48% predicted.
correlates.workup: Echocardiogram: estimated right ventricular systolic pressure 62 mmHg with a dilated right ventricle; chest film and lung volumes normal.

correlates.name: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
correlates.presentation: A 38-year-old office manager who smokes 2 packs a day has 3 months of dry cough, exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Few crackles, SpO2 94%. FEV1/FVC 0.80, DLCO 58%. Chest film: fine nodular and web-like markings in the upper and middle zones with the bases spared.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: sheets of cells with folded, lengthwise-grooved nuclei and pale cytoplasm mixed with eosinophils; S100+, CD1a+, langerin (CD207)+, CD68-. EM: rod-shaped cytoplasmic granules with a dilated end. Some carry a BRAF mutation.
correlates.management: Stop smoking; symptoms generally fade after cessation, while continued smoking scars and destroys the small airways.

correlates.name: Pulmonary nocardiosis
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old kidney transplant recipient on tacrolimus and prednisone who gardens daily. Three weeks of fever, productive cough and a 4-kg weight loss, then 2 days of headache and new left arm weakness. T 38.4 C, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94%; crackles at the right apex.
correlates.workup: Chest CT: several nodules, some cavitating; brain MRI: a ring-enhancing lesion. Sputum: gram-positive branching filaments that are weakly acid-fast with a mild decolorizer; aerobic and catalase-positive.
correlates.management: A sulfonamide (TMP-SMX); image the brain, since spread there (and to skin) is common.

correlates.name: Q fever
correlates.presentation: 42-year-old sheep farmer who helped deliver lambs in the barn the week before. Two days of severe headache, chills, muscle aches and a dry cough. T 39.4 C, HR 96, RR 20, SpO2 95%; crackles at the right base; tender liver edge.
correlates.workup: Sputum Gram stain: inflammatory cells only, no organisms seen (the organism is intracellular and stains poorly). Chest film: patchy right lower zone infiltrate. ALT 140 U/L.
correlates.management: Doxycycline. Follow patients with valve disease or immune suppression: years later the infection can return as subacute endocarditis with negative blood cultures.

correlates.name: Reflex incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 36-year-old man 8 months after a T8 spinal cord injury from a motorcycle crash empties his bladder suddenly and without any warning sensation several times a day; he cannot tell when it is about to happen. Spastic legs; sensation absent below the nipples.
correlates.workup: Urodynamics: the bladder contracts on its own at low volume with no sensation of filling and no voluntary inhibition; postvoid residual varies.

correlates.name: REM sleep behavior disorder
correlates.presentation: A 67-year-old man's wife has moved to another room: some nights, mostly in the early-morning hours, he shouts, punches and kicks as if fighting, and once struck her. When woken he describes a vivid dream of being attacked. He is alert by day; neuro exam normal.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: in periods with bursts of rapid eye movements and a low-voltage mixed-frequency EEG, chin EMG tone stays high and the limbs jerk, instead of the chin going flat.

correlates.name: Renal AL amyloidosis
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old woman followed for an M protein on serum electrophoresis, with free light chains in her urine: 2 months of frothy urine and ankle swelling. BP 128/78. UA 4+ protein, no blood. 24-h protein 9 g, albumin 2.0 g/dL.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: amorphous pink deposits in the mesangium and vessel walls, salmon-pink with Congo red and green under polarized light; immunostain lambda-positive, kappa-negative; 8-10 nm fibrils on EM

correlates.name: Renal colic from an obstructing ureteral calculus
correlates.presentation: A 25-year-old man has his first-ever waves of sharp, cramping pain from the left groin up to the left flank, back and testicle, 8/10 despite OTC analgesics, with nausea, vomiting, frequency and urgency. No past stones or bowel disease. Afebrile; left flank tender; testes normal.
correlates.workup: Urinalysis: microscopic hematuria, no white cells, nitrite negative; BMP normal. Non-contrast CT: a 4 mm dense stone at the left ureterovesical junction, with the ureter and renal pelvis dilated above it.
correlates.management: NSAID first (ketorolac or ibuprofen). Size decides: 5 mm or less usually passes; >5-10 mm add an alpha blocker; >10 mm likely needs a procedure. Home if fluids down, pain controlled, no fever: strain urine; urology if not out by 4 weeks.

correlates.name: Renal infarction
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man 3 weeks after a large anterior MI that left a poorly moving apical wall: sudden left flank pain. Afebrile, BP 150/90, left costovertebral angle tenderness. UA microscopic blood. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Echocardiogram: mural thrombus in the left ventricle. Pathology: pale, wedge-shaped zone of coagulative necrosis with its base at the cortex; dead tubules keep their outlines but have no nuclei, rimmed by inflammation

correlates.name: Renal osteodystrophy (secondary hyperparathyroidism)
correlates.presentation: A 49-year-old man on hemodialysis for 6 years, who often skips his meal-time pills, has had a week of tingling around his mouth and painful cramping of his hands. BP 150/90, HR 78. ECG: QTc 520 ms.
correlates.workup: Calcium 7.2 mg/dL, phosphate 7.8 mg/dL, PTH 640 pg/mL, low activated vitamin D. Hand films: small punched-out lucent spots where mineral is no longer deposited.
correlates.management: Limit dietary phosphate to 800 mg/day or less (improves the parathyroid drive even though serum phosphate barely moves), give phosphate binders with meals, and keep nephrology involved.

correlates.name: Respiratory bronchiolitis-associated ILD
correlates.presentation: A 42-year-old man who currently smokes a pack a day (25 pack-years) has a year of mild cough and gradually increasing breathlessness on stairs. A few scattered crackles, no clubbing. FVC 82% predicted, DLCO 68%.
correlates.workup: Lung biopsy: brown-pigmented macrophages packed in the lumens of first- and second-order bronchioles just proximal to the alveolar ducts, with collagen around those bronchioles; the alveoli beyond are spared.
correlates.management: Smoking cessation alone; symptoms and lung function improve once he quits.

correlates.name: Restless legs syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman has 8 months of trouble falling asleep. Most evenings, once she lies down or sits through a film, a deep crawling ache in both calves makes her get up and pace; it settles while she walks and returns when she stops. Tired by day; neuro exam and pulses normal.
correlates.management: A dopamine agonist (pramipexole or ropinirole), long the drug of choice; gabapentin also eases symptoms and a benzodiazepine can improve sleep quality. Opioids are not a routine choice.

correlates.name: Rhabdomyolysis
correlates.presentation: A deconditioned 34-year-old woman comes to urgent care with aching pain in both thighs that has not eased in the 5 days since her first-ever indoor cycling class. Vitals are normal; both quadriceps are tender to touch. Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Creatine kinase 25,000 U/L five days after the exertion (about 5,000 is the level that prompts admission); muscle-pigment casts in the urine sediment.
correlates.management: Admit for IV fluids and diuresis to flush muscle breakdown products from the tubules. Do not add sodium bicarbonate: it reduces urinary casts but does not change kidney injury or mortality.

correlates.name: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes admitted in ketoacidosis (glucose 540 mg/dL, pH 7.10). Three days of nasal stuffiness, right sinus pain and headache, now swelling around the right eye, double vision and a black patch of dead tissue on the right palate. T 38.5 C, HR 118.
correlates.workup: Biopsy of the palate lesion: wide, thick-walled, ribbon-like hyphae without septa, branching at right angles and invading vessel walls, with surrounding necrosis. Culture is difficult and often fails.
correlates.management: Emergency surgical debridement plus IV amphotericin B, while correcting the ketoacidosis.

correlates.name: Rib fractures with pulmonary contusion
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old driver hit the steering wheel in a high-speed crash. He has sharp left chest wall pain on every breath, bruising and point tenderness over the left 5th-8th ribs, and coughs a little blood. RR 26, HR 112, BP 118/76, SpO2 90%.
correlates.workup: Film: gaps in the cortex of four adjacent left ribs where they no longer line up, without callus; directly beneath them a patchy white airspace opacity that does not respect lobar borders.
correlates.management: More than 3 acute rib breaks generally means admission for observation rather than discharge.

correlates.name: Right mainstem intubation
correlates.presentation: A 70-year-old woman is intubated in the ED for respiratory failure. Twenty minutes later SpO2 falls to 86% and peak airway pressure rises; breath sounds are present on the right but absent on the left, and the left chest barely moves. Trachea midline, BP 128/74.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: the tube's radiopaque marker lies beyond the carina inside the right main bronchus; the entire left lung is uniformly white with volume loss, while the right lung is aerated.
correlates.management: Pull the tube back until the tip sits at least 2 cm above the carina (about the level of the clavicular heads, allowing for neck movement), then repeat the film.

correlates.name: Right middle lobe pneumonia
correlates.presentation: A 6-year-old boy has 3 days of fever to 39.4 C and cough. RR 34, HR 128, SpO2 94%; crackles and bronchial breath sounds over the right anterior chest beside the sternum.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: fluffy opacity beside the heart erasing the right heart border; left heart border and right hemidiaphragm stay sharp; no volume loss; air-filled bronchi within it. Lateral: wedge over the heart with two straight fissure edges.

correlates.name: RSV bronchiolitis in an infant
correlates.presentation: 4-month-old in January whose 3-year-old sister has a cold. Three days of runny nose and cough, now fast breathing and feeding poorly. T 38.0 C, HR 162, RR 64, SpO2 91%; nasal flaring, intercostal retractions, wheezes on breathing out and fine crackles in both lungs.
correlates.workup: Rapid antigen test on nasal secretions positive; multiplex PCR confirms. Diagnosis otherwise rests on age, winter season and the exam.
correlates.management: Supportive care; ribavirin only in select severe cases. Prevention for high-risk infants: a monoclonal antibody shot in the first RSV season, or vaccinating the mother in pregnancy.

correlates.name: Salicylate overdose
correlates.presentation: A 24-year-old woman with chronic migraines has had more frequent headaches for weeks and treats them with over-the-counter pills. Her husband brings her in confused, her breathing 'looks uncomfortable'. RR 34, HR 116. Na+ 140, Cl- 104, HCO3- 13.
correlates.workup: ABG 2 hours after ingestion: pH 7.53, PaCO2 24, HCO3- 21. ABG at 10 hours: pH 7.41, PaCO2 20, HCO3- 12, anion gap 24.
correlates.management: Activated charcoal; gastric lavage only for a massive ingestion under 30 minutes old; IV sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize the urine (not the serum) and speed excretion; dialysis if severe.

correlates.name: Sarcoidosis
correlates.presentation: A 31-year-old Black woman, a schoolteacher, has 2 months of dry cough, exertional dyspnea, fatigue, night sweats and painful red nodules on both shins. T 37.9 C, SpO2 95%, lungs clear. Serum Ca 10.9 mg/dL; 24-h urine Ca raised; ESR 48 mm/h.
correlates.workup: Chest film: large symmetric nodes at both hila. Transbronchial biopsy: tight clusters of epithelioid macrophages and giant cells, no necrosis; AFB and fungal cultures negative. BAL CD4:CD8 6:1; tuberculin test anergic; serum ACE high.
correlates.management: Rule out tuberculosis and fungal infection first. Many remit on their own; for active or progressive disease give prednisone, and follow serum ACE to gauge response.

correlates.name: Sclerosing retroperitoneal fibrosis
correlates.presentation: 60-year-old man who takes an ergot derivative for migraines: 2 months of dull low back and flank pain and less urine. BP 154/94. Creatinine 3.0 mg/dL (1.0 a year ago). Ultrasound: both kidneys and upper ureters dilated; bladder empties fully.
correlates.workup: CT: a rind of tissue beginning at the sacral promontory, wrapping the lower abdominal aorta and spreading laterally to encase both ureters. Biopsy: dense collagen with many lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils

correlates.name: Secondary (reactivation) tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man born in India, living in a homeless shelter, with poorly controlled diabetes. Three months of productive cough, blood-streaked sputum, drenching night sweats and an 8-kg weight loss. T 38.2 C, BMI 17; wasted, clubbed; rhonchi at the right apex.
correlates.workup: Chest film: right upper lobe (apical-posterior) infiltrate with a 3-cm cavity and an air-fluid level. Three sputum samples: red rods on acid-fast stain, NAAT positive; culture turns positive after several weeks.
correlates.management: Negative-pressure room, N95 for staff. Start rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol + pyridoxine for 2 months, then isoniazid + rifampin for 4 months, without waiting for culture; directly observed therapy.

correlates.name: Secondary bacterial pneumonia after influenza
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old woman in January who had abrupt fever, muscle aches and dry cough 8 days ago and was getting better; now 2 days of new high fever, rigors, purulent sputum and right pleuritic pain. T 39.6 C, HR 118, RR 28, BP 92/58, SpO2 89%; crackles and dullness at the right base.
correlates.workup: WBC 19,400/uL with left shift; chest film: new right lower lobe consolidation; sputum Gram stain: gram-positive cocci in clusters; blood cultures drawn (all inpatients).
correlates.management: Admit; blood cultures; beta-lactam plus macrolide (or a respiratory fluoroquinolone), plus vancomycin or linezolid to cover methicillin-resistant cocci.

correlates.name: Secondary nocturnal enuresis
correlates.presentation: A 6-year-old girl who was reliably dry at night from age 4 has wet the bed most nights for the past 2 weeks. Her parents brought home a new baby a month ago and argue often. No daytime symptoms, fever or thirst. Exam normal.
correlates.management: Take a careful home and school history for the stressor (new sibling, conflict, a move, bullying), and rule out a urinary infection with a urinalysis and culture. Psychosocial cause until shown otherwise.

correlates.name: Serotonin syndrome from linezolid and an SSRI
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman on sertraline for depression began an oral antibiotic 2 days ago for vancomycin-resistant enterococcal bacteremia. Now agitated, sweating, with diarrhea; T 39.6 C, HR 128, BP 150/90; tremor, myoclonic jerks, brisk reflexes and sustained ankle clonus
correlates.management: Treat as an emergency: stop both serotonergic drugs, cool and give benzodiazepines for agitation as needed, and start cyproheptadine (a 5-HT2A antagonist)

correlates.name: Severe COVID-19 with ARDS
correlates.presentation: 61-year-old unvaccinated man with obesity and diabetes; positive home antigen test 9 days ago for fever, cough and muscle aches; now worsening breathlessness. T 38.6 C, HR 112, RR 34, SpO2 84% on a 15-L non-rebreather mask; crackles throughout both lungs.
correlates.workup: Nasal swab RT-PCR positive. ABG on FiO2 0.8: PaO2 88 mmHg (ratio 110); bilateral opacities not explained by effusion or collapse; normal LV on echo. Autopsy: hyaline membranes plus microvessel thrombi.
correlates.management: Intubate; tidal volume 4-8 mL/kg with high PEEP, prone positioning, cautious fluids; add dexamethasone; anticoagulate when critically ill. Inhaled nitric oxide raises SpO2 but not survival.

correlates.name: Severe obstructive sleep apnea with obesity
correlates.presentation: A 54-year-old man, BMI 39, neck 18.5 in, is drowsy all day despite 8 hours in bed and dozed at a red light. His wife hears loud snoring broken by silent pauses, then a gasp. BP 164/98 on three drugs; atrial fibrillation hard to control. Large tongue, crowded throat.
correlates.workup: Overnight study: 46 events/h. Nasal and oral airflow stop for 15-40 s while the chest and abdominal belts keep moving; SpO2 falls 96% to 86% and each event ends in an EEG arousal. No slow-wave (delta) stage, little REM.
correlates.management: CPAP nightly: room air (not oxygen) under pressure splints the pharynx open, often with a large REM rebound; it can ease resistant BP and AF. Weight loss; tirzepatide is approved for moderate-severe disease with excess weight.

correlates.name: Severe subcutaneous emphysema
correlates.presentation: A 45-year-old with a left chest tube for a traumatic pneumothorax develops swelling of the chest wall, neck and face over 12 hours until his eyes are puffed shut. The skin crackles under the fingers from the eyelids to the abdomen. BP 130/82, SpO2 94%.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: gas density throughout the soft tissues of the chest wall, neck and axillae, separating the fibres of the pectoral muscles into fine white streaks; the tubes and lines are a distraction from this finding.

correlates.name: Sickle cell nephropathy
correlates.presentation: 22-year-old Black man with lifelong anemia and repeated admissions for bone pain: 2 days of gross hematuria; he has always passed large volumes and wakes to urinate at night. BP 118/72. Urine osmolality 280 mOsm/kg after overnight fluid restriction. Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Urine fails to concentrate; hematuria. Pathology: patchy necrosis of the renal papillae, which turn yellow-white, from red cells occluding vessels in the hypoxic, hypertonic medulla

correlates.name: Silicosis complicated by tuberculosis
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old quarry driller with 6 years of known upper-zone nodular lung scarring has 6 weeks of fever, drenching night sweats, 5-kg weight loss and cough with blood-streaked sputum. T 38.3 C, HR 104, SpO2 93%.
correlates.workup: Sputum: acid-fast bacilli on smear; culture grows slow-growing mycobacteria at 4 weeks. Film: a new cavitating upper-zone opacity on a background of small calcified nodules and calcium-rimmed hilar nodes.

correlates.name: Simple coal workers' pneumoconiosis
correlates.presentation: A 57-year-old man who has worked underground in a West Virginia mine for 30 years has a chronic cough with daily sputum and mild exertional dyspnea; never smoked. SpO2 95%. FEV1/FVC 0.72, FVC 90% predicted, DLCO 82%. Film: many small rounded opacities, upper zones first.
correlates.workup: Lung sections: black star-shaped aggregates up to 4 mm of dust-laden macrophages around the bronchioles, with reticulin and little collagen, each ringed by enlarged centriacinar airspaces; no masses over 1 cm.

correlates.name: Small cell lung cancer, limited disease
correlates.presentation: A 61-year-old woman with 50 pack-years has 6 weeks of cough and 4-kg weight loss; a mass seen 3 months ago has doubled. Na+ 138 mEq/L, Ca 9.4 mg/dL, cortisol normal. CT: 5-cm central right hilar mass. Biopsy: sheets of cells with scant cytoplasm and nuclear molding.
correlates.workup: Staging CT of the chest, liver and adrenals, brain MRI and bone scan: the hilar mass and enlarged right mediastinal nodes are all within the right hemithorax; liver, adrenals, brain and bones clear.
correlates.management: Curative intent, usually without surgery: polychemotherapy (cisplatin and etoposide) plus chest radiation, then prophylactic cranial irradiation if the tumor responds to the first chemotherapy.

workup: Non-small cell lung cancer, stage I-IIIA (resectable)

correlates.name: Small cell lung carcinoma with ectopic ACTH
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old woman with 40 pack-years has 3 months of weight gain over the trunk, a rounded flushed face, new coarse facial hair, thigh weakness and low mood. BP 168/98; K+ 2.9 mEq/L, HCO3- 32 mEq/L, glucose 214 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Plasma corticotropin markedly high; serum and 24-h urine cortisol high. CT: bulky hilar mass. Biopsy: small cells with scant cytoplasm and nuclear molding; chromogranin+, synaptophysin+; EM: dense-core neurosecretory granules.

workup: Small cell lung carcinoma with SIADH

correlates.name: Small cell lung carcinoma with SIADH
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old woman with 50 pack-years has 3 weeks of confusion, headache, nausea, cough and 5-kg weight loss. Euvolemic, no edema; BP 128/76. Na+ 121 mEq/L, serum osm 252 mOsm/kg, urine osm 520 mOsm/kg, urine Na+ 48 mEq/L; TSH and cortisol normal.
