correlates.workup: CT: large hilar mass with bulky mediastinal nodes and liver deposits. Biopsy: sheets of small blue cells, scant cytoplasm, nuclear molding, very high mitotic rate, necrosis; chromogranin+, synaptophysin+, cytokeratin+; TP53 and RB1 loss.

workup: Small cell lung carcinoma with ectopic ACTH

correlates.name: Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura
correlates.presentation: A 55-year-old woman, a librarian with no industrial or shipyard work history, has mild exertional dyspnea and a dry cough; the chest film shows a large, smooth, well-circumscribed mass abutting the right lower chest wall. No effusion, no weight loss, no fever.
correlates.workup: CT: well-circumscribed mass hanging from the surface of the lung on a stalk, not encasing it. Resection: dense collagenous spindle-cell tissue with cystic spaces; keratin negative; NAB2-STAT6 fusion gene detected.
correlates.management: Surgical excision of the stalked mass; nearly always benign, rarely malignant.

correlates.name: Solitary pulmonary nodule, high probability (>8 mm)
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old man who still smokes (40 pack-years) has no symptoms; a chest film before hernia repair shows a 1.5-cm round right upper lobe opacity that was not on a film taken 3 years ago. Afebrile, SpO2 96%, no clubbing or palpable nodes, weight stable.
correlates.workup: Chest CT extended through the liver and adrenals: a 16-mm solid peripheral lesion with irregular, spiculated margins and no calcification; no enlarged hilar or mediastinal nodes; liver and adrenals clear.
correlates.management: Large and high-risk, so go straight to tissue: CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy for a peripheral lesion (a central one gets bronchoscopy). Risks: pneumothorax, bleeding, pneumonia. Intermediate risk would get PET first.

workup: Non-small cell lung cancer, stage I-IIIA (resectable)

correlates.name: Solitary pulmonary nodule, low probability (<4 mm)
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old accountant who has never smoked, with no family history of lung cancer, has a 3-mm solid, smooth spot in the right lower lobe on a CT done after a car crash. No cough, hemoptysis or weight loss; exam normal.
correlates.management: No follow-up CT is needed. The same spot in a high-risk patient (smoker, over 40, family history, workplace fiber exposure) may get a repeat CT at 12 months.

correlates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old farmer who grew up wading in Nile irrigation canals in Egypt; blood in his urine on and off since childhood, now constant hematuria and 8 kg weight loss. Hb 10.2 g/dL. Cystoscopy: a large ulcerated mass.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: invasive keratinizing carcinoma arising from dysplastic lining amid chronic inflammation, with eggs bearing a terminal spine lodged in the wall

correlates.name: Squamous cell lung carcinoma with hypercalcemia
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old man with 45 pack-years has 2 months of cough, blood-streaked sputum, constipation, polyuria and new confusion. BP 132/80, dry mucosa. Serum Ca 14.9 mg/dL, phosphate 2.3 mg/dL, PTH low, sodium and potassium normal.
correlates.workup: CT: central mass obstructing the right main bronchus with a necrotic, cavitating centre. Bronchoscopic biopsy: keratinizing nests with keratin pearls and intercellular bridges; TTF-1 negative. Serum PTH-related peptide raised.

correlates.name: Status asthmaticus
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old with known asthma has worsened over 2 days despite three back-to-back albuterol nebulizers and IV methylprednisolone in the ED. Drowsy, hunched, using neck muscles, blue lips; RR 34, HR 130; systolic BP falls 18 mmHg on inspiration; breath sounds faint, no wheeze.
correlates.workup: ABG: pH 7.27, PaCO2 52, PaO2 60 mmHg; the PaCO2 was 31 mmHg on arrival 3 hours earlier. Peak flow too low to record.
correlates.management: IV corticosteroids and continuous inhaled beta-2 agonist; add IV magnesium and heliox (less dense gas passes narrowed airways); trial of CPAP or BiPAP; intubate if failing and ventilate with permissive hypercapnia until the airways relax.

correlates.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis
correlates.presentation: 8-year-old in March with 1 day of severe sore throat and fever; no cough, runny nose or red eyes. T 39.0 C, HR 118; swollen red tonsils with white exudate, tender enlarged anterior cervical nodes; uvula midline; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: FACE score 4 of 4 (fever > 100.4 F, anterior adenopathy, no cough, tonsillar exudate). Rapid antigen test positive; throat culture: beta-hemolytic, bacitracin-sensitive colonies on blood agar.
correlates.management: Score 4: penicillin without testing (erythromycin if allergic); 2-3: test, treat if positive; 0-1: symptom care, no test. Treat to prevent abscess, rheumatic heart disease and GN; a positive swab without symptoms is not treated.

correlates.name: Stress urinary incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 47-year-old woman with three vaginal deliveries (one 4.5 kg baby, a long second stage) leaks small spurts of urine when she coughs, sneezes, laughs or lifts her toddler, for 2 years. No warning sensation, no leaking at rest, normal daytime frequency. Periods now irregular.
correlates.workup: Office cough test with a full bladder: a spurt with each cough that stops when the cough stops. Urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 30 mL by ultrasound.
correlates.management: Pelvic floor physiotherapy (Kegels) and anti-leak devices first; estrogen if peri- or postmenopausal. Surgery is the main fix: mid-urethral sling, bladder neck suspension, periurethral bulking or an artificial sphincter.

correlates.name: Struvite stones (infection stones)
correlates.presentation: A 58-year-old woman with a neurogenic bladder from multiple sclerosis, who self-catheterizes, has had 5 urinary infections this year, a dull, persistent left flank ache and intermittent blood in her urine. Afebrile today; BP 134/82; mild left flank tenderness.
correlates.workup: Urine pH 8.0 with rectangular prism-shaped crystals; culture grows a urease-producing gram-negative rod. KUB: a large radiopaque branching stone filling the left renal pelvis and calyces.
correlates.management: Clear the infection with culture-directed antibiotics and remove the stone surgically (percutaneous nephrolithotomy for one this large); a recurrent infection-related stone is an elective indication. Bilateral disease risks kidney failure.

correlates.name: Superior sulcus tumor with sympathetic chain involvement
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old man with 50 pack-years has 3 months of deep right shoulder and upper chest pain and 4-kg weight loss. His right upper lid droops, the right pupil is smaller than the left, the right eye looks sunken, and the right side of his face does not sweat.
correlates.workup: Chest film and CT: a mass at the extreme right lung apex eroding the posterior first and second ribs and extending into the soft tissue at the root of the neck; biopsy may show any non-small cell type.

correlates.name: Superior vena cava syndrome
correlates.presentation: A 59-year-old woman with 45 pack-years has 3 weeks of swelling of her face, neck and both arms, worse when she bends forward or lies flat, with headache and a full feeling in her head. Plethoric face; dilated veins over the upper chest wall; legs not swollen. BP 142/86.
correlates.workup: Contrast CT: a right paratracheal and hilar mass compressing and invading the large vein draining the head and arms, with collateral veins across the chest wall.

correlates.name: Talaromycosis
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old man from northern Vietnam with HIV, never treated. Six weeks of fevers, a 9-kg weight loss and dozens of small skin papules, many with a dark necrotic center, over the face, trunk and arms. T 38.9 C, HR 110, RR 18; thin.
correlates.workup: CD4 25/uL. Skin scraping: elongated yeast cells, each divided by one dark central transverse septum (they split rather than bud). Culture confirms.

correlates.name: Tension pneumothorax
correlates.presentation: A 31-year-old man on a ventilator after a motorcycle crash with right rib injuries suddenly becomes hypotensive: BP 76/40, HR 138, SpO2 80%, peak airway pressure up sharply. Right breath sounds absent, right chest hyperresonant, trachea deviated to the left, neck veins distended.
correlates.workup: Frontal film: thin white line along the right chest with no lung markings beyond it and dark spaces between the right ribs; collapsed lung sits medially, and the heart is pushed wholly into the left chest, none of it right of the spine.
correlates.management: Needle decompression at once, then a chest tube; do not wait for imaging when the patient is in shock.

correlates.name: Testicular torsion
correlates.presentation: An 8-year-old boy came home from school 2 hours ago walking hunched over, holding his lower abdomen; he vomited once. The abdomen is soft and nontender, but the left testicle is swollen, very tender and sits higher than the right. HR 112, afebrile.
correlates.workup: Doppler ultrasound of the scrotum: no blood flow to the swollen left testicle; normal flow on the right.
correlates.management: Straight to the ER and urology - the testicle dies within hours of pain onset. Untwist it surgically and tack down BOTH testicles, since the free-hanging attachment is usually bilateral; do not wait for an afternoon clinic slot.

correlates.name: Thalidomide embryopathy
correlates.presentation: Newborn of a 24-year-old woman from Brazil treated for leprosy; she took an oral TNF-lowering, anti-angiogenic drug for painful red skin nodules in the first trimester, before she knew she was pregnant. Hands arise near the shoulders; long bones of all four limbs short or absent
correlates.management: Prevention: negative pregnancy tests before and during therapy and two forms of birth control for any patient who could conceive; never use the drug for first-trimester morning sickness

correlates.name: Thin basement membrane disease
correlates.presentation: 15-year-old boy has passed red urine now and then for a year. Hearing and vision normal; BP 114/70. UA 1+ blood, no protein, glucose or WBCs; creatinine 0.7 mg/dL. His mother and sister have the same urine finding and are otherwise well.
correlates.workup: Repeat urinalyses: isolated hematuria, no proteinuria; normal creatinine. EM: diffuse, uniform attenuation of the GBM along every capillary loop, with the lamina densa not split
correlates.management: No treatment needed: reassure the family that renal function usually stays normal, the outlook is excellent and progression to renal failure is not expected

correlates.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
correlates.presentation: 31-year-old woman, 3 days of fever, headache, confusion and brief left arm weakness; pinpoint bleeding spots on her legs. Temp 101.3 F, BP 138/84. Hb 8.1 g/dL, schistocytes on smear, platelets 14,000/uL, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL. No diarrhea.
correlates.workup: ADAMTS13 activity severely reduced, with an inhibitory autoantibody against it; schistocytes and very low platelets. Kidney, when involved: fibrin-stained thrombi in glomerular capillary loops
correlates.management: Urgent plasma exchange to remove the autoantibody, replacing with fresh frozen plasma to restore working enzyme; recombinant ADAMTS13 can also supply the enzyme, mainly in the inherited form

correlates.name: Torsion of the appendix testis
correlates.presentation: A 10-year-old boy has a day of right scrotal pain that built up gradually. The pain is confined to a pea-sized tender nodule at the upper pole of the right testicle. The rest of the testicle is nontender, not swollen and normally placed; afebrile, HR 90.
correlates.management: Symptomatic: NSAIDs and ice, and reassure - it is benign. If the picture is not this clearly localized, send for Doppler ultrasound to rule out a twisted testicle.

correlates.name: Transfusion-related acute lung injury
correlates.presentation: A 64-year-old woman receives 2 units of packed red cells for a hemoglobin of 6.8 g/dL after hip surgery. Two hours after the second unit she is suddenly breathless: T 38.3 C, RR 32, BP 96/58, SpO2 85% on air, crackles in both lungs, neck veins flat.
correlates.management: Stop the infusion and support oxygenation. The real treatment is prevention: give red cells and plasma only when clearly needed and as little as possible - every unit is a 'liquid transplant' that inflames the lung.

correlates.name: Tuberculous lymphadenitis
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman who emigrated from Nigeria 2 years ago, with 6 weeks of a painless, enlarging lump above the left clavicle, evening fevers and a 4-kg weight loss. T 37.9 C; firm, matted 3-cm left supraclavicular and posterior cervical nodes; lungs clear.
correlates.workup: Excisional node biopsy, done for suspected lymphoma: caseating granulomas with multinucleated giant cells and acid-fast rods; no malignant cells; culture grows after several weeks.

correlates.name: Tuberous sclerosis
correlates.presentation: 4-year-old boy whose mother felt a lump in his belly. Exam: pale oval patches on his back, small red papules over his nose and cheeks, a firm left flank mass. BP 104/66. Ultrasound: bright, echogenic masses in both kidneys.
correlates.workup: Biopsy: abnormal thick-walled vessels, smooth muscle and fat cells seen as empty round holes; germline loss-of-function variant in a tumor-suppressor gene, autosomal dominant

correlates.name: Typical community-acquired pneumonia (outpatient)
correlates.presentation: Healthy 41-year-old teacher; no recent hospital stay or antibiotics. Three days of fever, cough with yellow sputum and left-sided pain on deep breaths. T 38.4 C, HR 96, RR 20, BP 124/78, SpO2 96%; eating and drinking; dullness, crackles and loud breath sounds at the left base.
correlates.workup: Chest film: left lower lobe consolidation (CT only if the film is unclear). Sputum Gram stain and culture rarely done; blood cultures are reserved for admitted patients; no organism identified in most cases.
correlates.management: Treat at home with amoxicillin, doxycycline or a macrolide. With heart, lung or kidney disease, cancer treatment or alcoholism: amoxicillin-clavulanate or a cephalosporin plus a macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

correlates.name: Typical hemolytic uremic syndrome
correlates.presentation: 6-year-old ate undercooked burgers at a picnic; 5 days of cramps and bloody diarrhea, now pale, vomiting blood, barely urinating, with petechiae. BP 130/84. Hb 7.2 g/dL, platelets 38,000/uL, BUN 72 mg/dL, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Smear: fragmented red cells (schistocytes), high reticulocyte count, low platelets; BUN and creatinine high; UA blood, protein and casts; stool grows E. coli O157:H7. Biopsy: glomerular capillaries plugged by fresh thrombi
correlates.management: Supportive care: IV fluids, red cell transfusion and dialysis for renal failure. Do not give antibiotics - killing the bacteria all at once releases a large load of Shiga toxin

correlates.name: Uncomplicated seasonal influenza
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old elementary-school teacher in late January; many pupils are off sick. Abrupt onset 30 hours ago of fever, chills, dry cough, severe muscle aches, headache and sore throat. T 39.2 C, HR 108, RR 18, SpO2 97%; lungs clear.
correlates.management: Start oseltamivir within 48 hours of onset (preferred, also in pregnancy): shortens illness by 1-2 days and cuts shedding. Alternatives: inhaled zanamivir (not with asthma/COPD), IV peramivir, one oral dose of baloxavir.

correlates.name: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
correlates.presentation: 6-week-old boy with fever 39.2 C, poor feeding and a urine culture growing E. coli; prenatal ultrasound showed a dilated left kidney. Ultrasound now: left renal pelvis and calyces markedly dilated, left ureter normal caliber, bladder and right kidney normal.
correlates.workup: VCUG: no reflux and a normal urethra. Resected segment: disorganized smooth muscle bundles with excess collagen laid down between them (a few cases: an aberrant renal vessel compressing from outside)
correlates.management: Treat the infection, then investigate further and correct the obstruction surgically if needed

correlates.name: Urethral caruncle
correlates.presentation: 79-year-old woman with 2 months of spotting on her underwear: a small, red, painful mass at the external urinary opening that bleeds when touched. No weight loss. UA a few RBCs.
correlates.workup: Excision: inflamed granulation tissue beneath a friable mucosa that may ulcerate; no malignant cells
correlates.management: Surgical excision is curative

correlates.name: Urethritis (sexually transmitted)
correlates.presentation: An 18-year-old man has 3 days of burning when he urinates, itching at the tip of the penis and pus at the urethral opening, a week after unprotected sex with a new partner. No urgency or frequency, no fever. Suprapubic area barely tender; no flank tenderness.
correlates.workup: Urine culture: low colony count, reported as 'sterile' or mixed genital flora. Gram stain of the discharge shows neutrophils, some containing gram-negative diplococci; swab and urine sent for STI testing.

correlates.name: Urge incontinence
correlates.presentation: A 66-year-old woman has a sudden, overwhelming need to void many times a day and often wets herself, sometimes a large amount, before she reaches the bathroom; she wakes 3 times a night. No leaking with coughing or lifting. Neuro exam normal; BMI 34.
correlates.workup: Urinalysis normal; postvoid residual 40 mL. Filling cystometry: involuntary detrusor contractions at 120 mL that reproduce her symptom and leak.
correlates.management: Lifestyle first (diet, weight loss, Kegels), then mainly medication: an anticholinergic, with care in the elderly (crosses the blood-brain barrier; not in closed-angle glaucoma). If that fails: botulinum toxin or sacral nerve modulation.

correlates.name: Uric acid stones
correlates.presentation: A 52-year-old roofer in Phoenix, who drinks little water on the job and eats red meat at most meals, comes to clinic after passing his second kidney stone in a year. Afebrile, BP 136/86, exam unremarkable. Serum urate 9.6 mg/dL; creatinine 1.0 mg/dL.
correlates.workup: Urine pH 5.0 with rhomboid plate-shaped crystals, some clustered in rosettes. The plain film shows no stone, but non-contrast CT shows a 6 mm stone in the left ureter.
correlates.management: Alkalinize the urine and give allopurinol to lower urinary urate; raise fluid intake for more urine volume and cut back on purine-rich meats.

correlates.name: Urinary retention
correlates.presentation: A 76-year-old woman was started on oxybutynin for frequent voiding 3 days ago. For 14 hours she has passed no urine and has painful lower abdominal swelling. Afebrile; BP 158/90. Lower abdomen distended, tender above the pubis, dull to percussion up toward the umbilicus.
correlates.workup: Bladder ultrasound: 1,100 mL in the bladder; creatinine 1.3 mg/dL (0.9 baseline); urinalysis normal.
correlates.management: Decompress the bladder with a urethral catheter now and stop the anticholinergic (alpha agonists and calcium channel blockers do this too); admit when an obstructed bladder needs a catheter.

correlates.name: Urinary schistosomiasis
correlates.presentation: A 19-year-old who grew up in rural Egypt swimming and washing in an irrigation canal moved to the US last year. For months he has seen visible blood in his urine, with mild burning and suprapubic fullness. Vitals normal; exam unremarkable.
correlates.workup: Urine sediment: large oval eggs, each with a sharp spine at one end. Routine urine culture: no growth.

correlates.name: Urothelial carcinoma in situ
correlates.presentation: 66-year-old man, 40 pack-years: microscopic hematuria on two urinalyses; urine cytology shows malignant cells. Cystoscopy: multifocal patches of red, granular, slightly thickened bladder mucosa, with no mass anywhere.
correlates.workup: Biopsy of the red patches: flat lining with full-thickness atypia, enlarged pleomorphic cells with visible nucleoli that lose cohesion and shed; no invasion; p53 and RB pathway mutations

correlates.name: Urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
correlates.presentation: 70-year-old man, 50 pack-years, who took analgesics daily for years: three episodes of painless visible hematuria. BP 136/82. Hb 13.1 g/dL. CT: irregular soft-tissue mass in the left renal pelvic cavity and calyces with hydronephrosis.
correlates.workup: Ureteroscopic biopsy: fibrovascular cores covered by transitional cells with markedly pleomorphic nuclei, as in bladder tumors; deeply invasive tumors carry a 17p deletion with p53 mutation

correlates.name: UTI in a nursing-home resident
correlates.presentation: An 86-year-old woman in long-term care, incontinent and left in soiled briefs for hours, has 2 days of new confusion, poor appetite, feeling cold and shaking chills; no burning. T 35.8 C, HR 108, BP 104/60. No Foley. Dipstick: nitrite and leukocyte esterase positive.
correlates.management: Send a urine culture with sensitivities before choosing, then use the narrowest drug that covers the isolate: resistant E. coli, Pseudomonas, enterococci, staph and Candida are common in this setting, and broad agents breed C. difficile.

correlates.name: UTI in pregnancy
correlates.presentation: A 27-year-old woman at 14 weeks' gestation feels well at her prenatal visit. A screening clean-catch culture grows more than 100,000 CFU/mL of a gram-negative rod, the same strain on a repeat specimen. No dysuria, frequency, fever or flank pain. BP 110/68, T 36.8 C.
correlates.management: Treat even without symptoms: 7 days of amoxicillin (penicillin allergy: nitrofurantoin or a third-generation cephalosporin). If fever and flank pain develop, start IV or IM in hospital, finish 10 days orally, reculture 5 days after.

correlates.name: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 67-year-old man with asthma, intubated in the ICU for respiratory failure. At 72 hours he spikes T 38.6 C (101.5 F), needs FiO2 raised from 0.4 to 0.7, and thick yellow secretions are suctioned from the endotracheal tube. HR 112, BP 104/62; coarse crackles in both lungs.
correlates.workup: WBC 20,000/uL with 80% neutrophils (against a viral cause); chest film: new bilateral infiltrates. Endotracheal aspirate or BAL: gram-positive cocci in clusters, catalase- and coagulase-positive. Cultures sent before antibiotics.
correlates.management: Blood and lower-airway cultures, then empiric antibiotics at once by the hospital antibiogram: vancomycin or linezolid plus an antipseudomonal agent; de-escalate early. Prevent: head of bed 30-45 degrees, less sedation, early extubation.

correlates.name: Vesicoureteral reflux
correlates.presentation: A 3-year-old girl has her third febrile kidney infection in a year; between infections she is well, toilet-trained and voids with a normal stream. BP 98/60; abdomen soft without masses. Renal ultrasound: right renal pelvis and the whole right ureter dilated; bladder normal.
correlates.workup: Voiding study (catheter, contrast, continuous films while she voids): contrast rises from the bladder up the right ureter into a dilated pelvis and calyces; the higher the grade, the more dilated and the more kidney damage.
correlates.management: Grade by the voiding study: grades 1-2 watch and wait (often outgrown; low-dose prophylactic antibiotics if infections recur); grade 3 decide with pediatric urology; grades 4-5 surgery. Every infection adds kidney damage.

correlates.name: Vesicovaginal or ureterovaginal fistula
correlates.presentation: A 46-year-old woman, 3 weeks after an abdominal hysterectomy, is wet all the time, day and night: urine drips continuously with no urge and no relation to coughing or lifting. She still voids some urine normally. Afebrile; no flank pain.
correlates.management: Largely preventable at surgery: identify the ureters and take the bladder down during hysterectomy or C-section. These rarely arise on their own - a constantly wet patient after pelvic surgery or trauma is this until proved otherwise.

correlates.name: Viral hemorrhagic cystitis (immunocompromised)
correlates.presentation: A 34-year-old man 6 weeks after an allogeneic stem cell transplant for leukemia, on tacrolimus, has 3 days of bright red urine with clots, painful urgent voiding and suprapubic pain. T 37.4 C, BP 126/78, platelets 140,000.
correlates.workup: Routine bacterial urine culture: no growth. Urine testing finds a polyomavirus that most people pick up in childhood and then carry latently.

correlates.name: Vocal cord paralysis
correlates.presentation: A 50-year-old man who never smoked had childhood polio that weakened his swallowing and speech muscles; he now has exertional dyspnea. Lungs clear, SpO2 97%. FEV1/FVC 0.79, FEV1 88% predicted.
correlates.workup: Flow-volume loop: the inspiratory limb is cut off into a flat plateau while the expiratory limb is normal. Laryngoscopy: the right side of the glottis does not move and the left moves only partly.

correlates.name: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome
correlates.presentation: 34-year-old woman with bilateral renal masses and renal cysts on CT; a cerebellar vascular tumor was removed 3 years ago and she has a retinal vascular tumor. Her father had an adrenal tumor that caused spells of headache, sweating and very high BP.
correlates.workup: Renal tumors: cells with empty-looking cytoplasm in a delicate vascular network. Germline loss of a chromosome 3p tumor suppressor that normally targets HIF-1, so VEGF-driven angiogenesis rises

correlates.name: VRE infection
correlates.presentation: 70-year-old woman in the ICU for 3 weeks after a perforated bowel, treated with several courses of cephalosporins and vancomycin, with a central venous catheter. New fever and chills. T 38.9 C, HR 114, BP 94/58; catheter site clean; no new murmur.
correlates.workup: Blood cultures: gram-positive cocci in chains, catalase-negative, turning bile esculin black and growing in 6.5% NaCl; the isolate is not inhibited by vancomycin and is resistant to cephalosporins.
correlates.management: Contact isolation (single room, gloves, gown) to stop spread to other ICU patients. Treat with linezolid (100% oral bioavailability; watch blood counts and SSRIs); cephalosporins select for these strains.

correlates.name: Wilms tumor
correlates.presentation: 3-year-old girl whose father felt a large lump in her belly during a bath; she seems well. BP 128/84, high for age. Smooth, firm left flank mass that stops short of the midline. UA microscopic blood. CT: 10 cm circumscribed solid mass arising within the left kidney.
correlates.workup: Resection: soft tan-gray mass with a smooth pseudocapsule; histology in three parts: sheets of small, crowded blue blastemal cells, loose or myxoid stroma, and primitive tubules
correlates.management: Nephrectomy plus chemotherapy; prognosis is good even with lung metastases at diagnosis, but anaplasia (TP53) predicts resistance to chemotherapy

correlates.name: Zanamivir bronchospasm
correlates.presentation: 45-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55% predicted) and 1 day of fever, myalgia and dry cough took his first dose of an inhaled dry-powder influenza antiviral. Within 30 minutes: chest tightness, RR 26, SpO2 88% on room air, prolonged expiration with diffuse wheezes
correlates.management: Stop the inhaled powder and give a short-acting bronchodilator; switch to oral oseltamivir. This inhaled antiviral is not recommended in asthma or COPD

glomerular.name: Alport syndrome
glomerular.lightMicro: Trichrome: lipid-laden foam cells in the interstitium between tubules and glomeruli
glomerular.electronMicro: Lamina densa split and laminated into many interwoven strands; GBM irregularly thick and thin
glomerular.clue: Boy aged 5-20; X-linked COL4A5 (alpha-5 type IV collagen) in 85%; sensorineural hearing loss, eye abnormalities and a family history of renal failure; progresses to ESKD

glomerular.name: Anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome)
glomerular.lightMicro: Acute GN with crescents filling Bowman's space: fibrin, parietal epithelial cells, monocytes and macrophages compressing the tuft
glomerular.immunofluor: Smooth, continuous linear IgG with C3 tracing every glomerular basement membrane
glomerular.electronMicro: No electron-dense deposits; GBM wrinkled with focal breaks in its continuity
glomerular.clue: Men in their late 20s; IgG against the NC1 domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen in glomerular and lung capillaries; hemoptysis first, then renal failure; plasmapheresis

glomerular.name: Collapsing FSGS
glomerular.lightMicro: PAS: the glomerular tuft is shrunken and retracted with its capillary loops closed, capped by enlarged, crowded podocytes and parietal epithelial cells
glomerular.clue: Untreated retroviral infection with a low CD4 count, or certain drugs and microvascular injury; heavy proteinuria; the worst prognosis of the podocyte-scarring lesions

glomerular.name: Dense deposit disease (MPGN type II)
glomerular.lightMicro: Thick capillary walls plus increased mesangial and endocapillary cells; silver stain splits the GBM into two parallel lines
glomerular.immunofluor: Granular C3 with properdin; IgG, C1q and C4 usually absent
glomerular.electronMicro: A continuous ribbon of very electron-opaque material inside the GBM itself, splitting the membrane
glomerular.clue: Children or adults; an autoantibody (C3 nephritic factor) stabilizes the alternative-pathway C3 convertase; low C3, factor B and properdin with normal C1 and C4

glomerular.name: Diabetic nephropathy
glomerular.lightMicro: Round PAS- and trichrome-positive nodules of mesangial matrix; afferent and efferent arteriolar walls replaced by glassy hyaline; thickened GBM
glomerular.immunofluor: Nonspecific staining, with no granular or linear immune pattern
glomerular.electronMicro: Markedly thickened, homogeneous GBM that has lost its separate lamina densa and lamina lucida; foot process effacement
glomerular.clue: Long-standing poorly controlled type 1 (age 15-25) or type 2 diabetes; microalbuminuria first, then heavy proteinuria; retinopathy and hypertension; top cause of chronic renal failure in the US

glomerular.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
glomerular.lightMicro: Only some glomeruli are involved, and in each only part of the tuft is scarred, with glassy eosinophilic hyaline deposits; the rest of the tuft looks normal
glomerular.immunofluor: Usually negative; nonspecific IgM and C3 trapped only in the scarred parts of the tuft
glomerular.electronMicro: Diffuse foot process effacement with podocyte degeneration and detachment; no electron-dense deposits
glomerular.clue: Most common adult nephrotic cause in the US; Black and Hispanic adults; IV heroin, sickle cell disease, severe obesity; hypertension and microscopic hematuria; poor steroid response

glomerular.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
glomerular.lightMicro: Crescents in Bowman's space alongside necrotizing inflammation of small vessels packed with neutrophils; silver stain shows gaps where the GBM is destroyed
glomerular.immunofluor: Little or no immunoglobulin or complement staining despite active crescents
glomerular.electronMicro: No immune deposits; fragmented GBM with wrinkling and focal ruptures
glomerular.clue: Childhood to middle age; PR3 (cytoplasmic) ANCA; recurrent sinusitis, epistaxis and nasal septal ulcers or perforation, hemoptysis, lung infarcts

glomerular.name: IgA nephropathy
glomerular.lightMicro: PAS: mesangial matrix expanded and mesangial cells increased; capillary loops otherwise open and thin
glomerular.immunofluor: Large granular clumps of IgA with C3 and properdin, concentrated in the mesangium
glomerular.electronMicro: Electron-dense deposits within the mesangial matrix; capillary endothelium intact
glomerular.clue: Most common primary GN worldwide; males, peak age 20-30; recurrent gross hematuria within days of a respiratory or GI infection; high serum IgA; linked to celiac and liver disease

glomerular.name: Lupus nephritis, class I-II
glomerular.lightMicro: Glomeruli normal or showing only increased mesangial cells; capillary walls thin, no crescents
glomerular.immunofluor: Granular IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q confined to the mesangium
glomerular.electronMicro: Electron-dense deposits confined to the mesangium
glomerular.clue: Young woman with ANA and anti-dsDNA, low C3 and C4; mild hematuria or proteinuria while renal function is still preserved

glomerular.name: Lupus nephritis, class III-IV
glomerular.lightMicro: H&E: capillary walls thick, rigid and rounded with amorphous hyaline material; mesangial and endocapillary hypercellularity and crescents, in some or nearly all glomeruli
glomerular.immunofluor: Large granular chunks of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q along the capillary loops and in the mesangium
glomerular.electronMicro: Subendothelial electron-dense deposits just beneath the endothelium lining the lumen, plus mesangial deposits
glomerular.clue: Woman aged 15-44 with a facial rash, arthralgias and fatigue; ANA and anti-dsDNA positive; low C3 and C4; RBC casts, Cr 2.0; raised risk of progressing to end-stage disease

glomerular.name: Lupus nephritis, class V
glomerular.lightMicro: Uniform GBM thickening without any increase in glomerular cells
glomerular.immunofluor: Granular deposits along the GBM that stain for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q together
glomerular.electronMicro: Many subepithelial electron-dense deposits spread evenly along the whole outer surface of the GBM
glomerular.clue: Woman with a known anti-dsDNA-positive multisystem autoimmune disease (low C3 and C4) who develops leg edema and foamy urine with nephrotic-range proteinuria

glomerular.name: Lupus nephritis, class VI
glomerular.lightMicro: Global sclerosis: most glomeruli are scarred across the entire tuft and no longer function
glomerular.electronMicro: Immune deposits may no longer be seen because the glomeruli are so scarred
glomerular.clue: Many years of anti-dsDNA-positive autoimmune disease with rash and arthritis, now nonfunctioning end-stage kidneys on the way to dialysis

glomerular.name: Membranoproliferative GN type I
glomerular.lightMicro: Thick capillary walls plus increased mesangial and endocapillary cells; silver stain splits the GBM into two parallel lines
glomerular.immunofluor: Granular C3 with IgG, C1q and C4 in the mesangium and outlining the loops
glomerular.electronMicro: Subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits; mesangial cells grow into the capillary wall and split the GBM
glomerular.clue: Chronic hepatitis C, usually with cryoglobulins; children or adults; mixed nephritic-nephrotic urine with RBC casts; hypertension; most progress to CKD

glomerular.name: Membranous nephropathy
glomerular.lightMicro: Capillary walls diffusely and uniformly thickened with no increase in cells; silver stain shows GBM projections between the deposits
glomerular.immunofluor: Discrete granular IgG and C3 evenly outlining the capillary loops
glomerular.electronMicro: Subepithelial electron-dense deposits along the whole GBM, with new basement membrane projecting up between them; foot processes effaced
glomerular.clue: Men 30-50 (2:1); IgG against the phospholipase A2 receptor in 70% of primary cases; secondary to NSAIDs, captopril, hepatitis B/C, lung or colon cancer, lupus; renal vein thrombosis

glomerular.name: Minimal change disease
glomerular.lightMicro: Glomeruli look normal on PAS: thin capillary walls, open loops, normal mesangium; fat stains are positive in glomeruli and tubular cells
glomerular.immunofluor: Negative for every immunoglobulin and complement component
glomerular.electronMicro: Foot processes swollen and fused into one continuous sheet; GBM and endothelium normal; no electron-dense deposits
glomerular.clue: Most common nephrotic cause in children; follows a URI or vaccination (also NSAIDs, Hodgkin lymphoma); albumin is the main protein lost; normal BP; prompt steroid response

glomerular.name: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
glomerular.lightMicro: Diffusely enlarged, very cellular glomeruli: neutrophils and monocytes fill the tufts, endothelial and mesangial cells proliferate, few open loops; crescents if severe
glomerular.immunofluor: Coarse, irregular granular IgG and C3 scattered along capillary walls and in the mesangium
glomerular.electronMicro: Large discrete electron-dense deposits on the epithelial side of the GBM, beneath the foot processes; occasional mesangial deposits
glomerular.clue: Child aged 2-6, 1-4 weeks after a sore throat or skin infection; low C3 with normal C4; high ASO (anti-hyaluronidase after skin infection); 95% of children recover in 6-8 weeks

glomerular.name: Renal AL amyloidosis
glomerular.lightMicro: Amorphous pink material expanding the mesangium and vessel walls; salmon-pink with Congo red and green birefringence under polarized light
glomerular.immunofluor: Immunostain of the deposits: positive for lambda light chain, negative for kappa
glomerular.electronMicro: Fibrils 8-10 nm wide of misfolded protein deposited in the mesangium
glomerular.clue: Older adult with an M protein in serum and free light chains in urine; plasma-cell clone, lambda more often than kappa; new nephrotic syndrome

glomerular.name: Thin basement membrane disease
glomerular.lightMicro: Normal on light microscopy: glomeruli, tubules and interstitium unremarkable, with no extra cells
glomerular.electronMicro: Diffuse, uniform attenuation of the GBM along every capillary loop; the lamina densa is not split
glomerular.clue: Teen with intermittent red urine and isolated hematuria; mother and sister have the same and are otherwise well; autosomal dominant alpha-3/alpha-4 collagen IV; normal hearing; excellent prognosis

genes.name: Alport syndrome

genes.name: Alport syndrome

genes.name: Asthma

genes.card: IL-4/5/9/13 cluster, beta-adrenergic and glucocorticoid receptor genes · chromosome 5q

genes.name: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome

genes.card: Complement factor I or CD46 (membrane cofactor protein) mutation

genes.role: About half of cases: complement activation goes unchecked and injures endothelium, with no diarrheal prodrome and a worse course

genes.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
genes.role: Organomegaly, macroglossia, hemihypertrophy, omphalocele and enlarged adrenals, with raised childhood renal tumor risk
genes.card: Region alteration (taught as a deletion) · chromosome 11p15

genes.name: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma

genes.name: Denys-Drash syndrome
genes.role: About 90% develop a childhood renal embryonal tumor; with gonadal dysgenesis and renal failure from diffuse mesangial sclerosis

genes.name: Familial idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

genes.name: Familial idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
genes.role: Inherited telomerase defects (about 15% of familial cases) shorten telomeres, so alveolar epithelial cells die and cannot regenerate

genes.name: Hereditary papillary renal cell carcinoma
genes.role: Autosomal dominant gain of the growth-factor receptor gene, giving multiple bilateral tumors

genes.name: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
genes.role: Mucin gene variant that raises mucus secretion and alters mucociliary clearance; present in about one third of cases

genes.name: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
genes.role: Marks the tumors that have grown beyond the lining of the upper collecting system

genes.name: Lung adenocarcinoma

genes.name: Lung adenocarcinoma
genes.role: Receptor tyrosine kinase genes listed with EGFR, MET and RET as gain-of-function drivers of the glandular, TTF-1-positive type

genes.name: Lung adenocarcinoma
genes.role: In about 30%, more often in smokers; usually a worse prognosis, with targeted treatment still emerging

genes.name: Malignant mesothelioma

genes.name: Narcolepsy

genes.name: Noninvasive papillary urothelial carcinoma

genes.card: FGFR3 amplification with activating RAS and PI3-kinase mutations

genes.name: Papillary renal cell carcinoma

genes.card: Trisomies 7, 16 and 17; loss of Y in men (sporadic)

genes.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (hereditary)
genes.role: Macrophages need GM-CSF signaling to clear surfactant; 90% of cases are instead autoimmune, with antibodies against GM-CSF

genes.name: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
genes.role: Found in some smokers in their late 30s to early 40s with grooved, CD1a-positive cells; symptoms usually fade after quitting

genes.name: Small cell lung carcinoma
genes.role: MYC-family amplification joins the two tumor-suppressor losses in the chromogranin- and synaptophysin-positive tumor

genes.name: Small cell lung carcinoma
genes.gene: TP53 and RB1 loss of function
genes.role: Both tumor suppressors lost in this neuroendocrine tumor with the strongest tie to smoking
genes.card: TP53 and RB1 loss of function

genes.name: Solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura
genes.role: Unique fusion in a usually benign, pedunculated, keratin-negative mass that has nothing to do with asbestos

genes.name: Squamous cell lung carcinoma
genes.role: Cell-cycle brake lost in most of these keratinizing tumors, alongside p53

genes.name: Squamous cell lung carcinoma
genes.role: Growth factor receptor gain in the central, PTHrP-secreting tumor type

genes.name: Squamous cell lung carcinoma
genes.gene: TP53 mutation (highest rate of any lung cancer type)
genes.role: The single most important gene for this central, keratinizing, smoking-related tumor
genes.card: TP53 mutation (highest rate of any lung cancer type)

genes.name: Superficial urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
genes.role: Seen in noninvasive tumors of the pelvicalyceal lining; smoking is the big risk factor

genes.name: Thin basement membrane disease
genes.role: Alpha-3 or alpha-4 collagen chain change, dominant inheritance: hematuria runs in the family, without hearing or eye loss or familial kidney failure

genes.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
genes.gene: ADAMTS13 mutation (inherited; less common than autoantibody)
genes.role: Metalloproteinase that trims von Willebrand factor multimers; most cases are acquired autoantibodies, treated with plasma exchange
genes.card: ADAMTS13 mutation (inherited; less common than autoantibody)

genes.name: Tuberous sclerosis
genes.gene: TSC1 or TSC2 loss of function (autosomal dominant)
genes.role: Tumor suppressors that together restrain mTOR; renal angiomyolipomas in 25-50%, cardiac rhabdomyomas, retinal hamartomas, skin angiofibromas
genes.card: TSC1 or TSC2 loss of function (autosomal dominant) · chromosome 9q (TSC1), 16p (TSC2)

genes.name: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (flat pathway)
genes.role: High-grade, multifocal, confined to the epithelium at first, yet the precursor of most muscle-invasive bladder cancer

genes.name: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome
genes.gene: Germline VHL tumor suppressor mutation (autosomal dominant)
genes.role: Renal cysts and bilateral clear cell tumors with cerebellar and retinal hemangioblastomas and pheochromocytoma
genes.card: Germline VHL tumor suppressor mutation (autosomal dominant)

genes.name: WAGR syndrome
genes.role: About 33% develop a childhood renal embryonal tumor; absent irises, genital anomalies and developmental delay come with the deletion

genes.role: Seen in the undifferentiated, pleomorphic areas; these children tend to resist chemotherapy
avoid: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
